objectiveLabel: Translate business problems into Claude-based AI solutions

existing.scenario: Utility outage emails need faster triage while equipment switching stays outside model authority.
existing.evidence: 18,000 daily emails; target is 15-minute triage; operator retains switching.
existing.decisiveConstraint: The first release must convert the 15-minute triage goal into one bounded operator workflow, while breaker control remains outside Claude's authority.
existing.expectedDecision: Scope Claude to extract location and severity, retrieve the runbook, draft a triage summary, and route uncertain cases to an operator; define triage completion and classification acceptance criteria before expanding scope.
existing.rationale: This row owns the business-to-solution boundary: a narrow language workflow and an explicit exclusion for equipment switching. The transfer row separately owns measured bottleneck selection and supervisor review.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Launch a general chatbot and defer measurement until operators use it.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: A chat surface does not define the triage job, acceptance evidence, or authority boundary.
existing.counterfactual: If outage messages were already normalized and classification followed deterministic rules, choose a rules-and-queue workflow and reserve Claude for a separately evidenced unstructured explanation need.
existing.sourceSection: When (and when not) to use agents
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends starting with the simplest solution and adding agentic complexity only when it is needed, because agentic systems trade latency and cost for task performance.
existing.auditFinding: Underlying decision is sound, but the accepted option is strictly longest; rewrite options to comparable action scope. Keep this row on initial business-to-solution scope and exclude the returns transfer row's measured bottleneck and supervisor-review recipe.

existing.scenario: A hospital prototype is called a productivity assistant, but reviewers disagree and no current-process baseline exists.
existing.evidence: The request names an aspiration; the prototype can change before production funding.
existing.decisiveConstraint: A task, success measure, representative cases, and baseline are missing.
existing.expectedDecision: Define the scheduling task and empirical acceptance criteria before tuning prompts or architecture.
existing.rationale: Without an observable work unit and baseline, capability changes cannot prove business value.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Add tools or raise reasoning effort until reviewers agree.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: More capability cannot define productivity or create a reproducible comparison.
existing.counterfactual: If a baseline and labeled scheduling set already existed, the next decision could compare prompt or model variants instead of doing discovery.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic's guide says to establish clear success criteria and empirical tests before improving a prompt.
existing.auditFinding: The diagnostic principle is valid, but the accepted option is strictly longest and gives away the answer; rebalance option length and make the evidence distinction sharper.

existing.scenario: A benefits assistant must explain eligibility while deterministic, versioned income and date rules remain authoritative.
existing.evidence: Eligibility thresholds and formulas are reproducible; an incorrect approval has legal and financial impact.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Claude may interpret and explain evidence but cannot become the eligibility decision authority.
existing.expectedDecision: Extract facts and retrieve policy with Claude, then pass validated fields to a versioned rules engine.
existing.rationale: The design places probabilistic language work around a deterministic decision boundary that can be replayed and audited.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Let Claude read policy and issue the final approval in natural language.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: A fluent response cannot guarantee reproducible thresholds, formulas, or effective dates.
existing.counterfactual: If policy were advisory and approvals were nonbinding, Claude could answer directly; the stated legal consequence rules that out.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic describes the augmented LLM as an LLM enhanced with capabilities such as retrieval, tools, and memory, with interfaces tailored to the use case.
existing.auditFinding: The authority boundary is correct, but option a is strictly longest and the distractors are cartoonishly unsafe; rewrite options with comparable, credible alternatives.

existing.scenario: Returns leadership asks for 'automation,' but time studies show policy lookup consumes most staff time and supervisors already own refund approval.
existing.evidence: Case messages and policy versions are available; staff can label lookup time, recommendation corrections, and approval outcomes.
existing.decisiveConstraint: The first experiment must target the measured lookup bottleneck and make policy grounding observable before any authority expansion.
existing.expectedDecision: Pilot policy retrieval plus a structured recommendation only; set a stop criterion on grounded recommendation quality and lookup time, leaving approval unchanged.
existing.rationale: This turns an ambiguous automation request into a staged decision about the bottleneck and evidence, rather than treating all returns work as one automation target.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Optimize the number of conversations completed and add refund execution to prove automation value.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Conversation count ignores the measured lookup bottleneck, and refund execution changes authority before evidence supports it.
existing.counterfactual: If time study showed supervisor approval, rather than policy lookup, was the bottleneck and approvals were delegated, the first experiment would target that validated approval path.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends clear success criteria and empirical tests before prompt improvement, making the business objective testable.
existing.auditFinding: The original row repeated selection's generic outcome-plus-authority recipe; the revised decision now targets a measured policy-lookup bottleneck with a staged stop criterion.

additions.scenario: A utility billing team asks for Claude to classify 200,000 daily exception records; every required field is already normalized and the policy is a deterministic rules table.
additions.evidence: Inputs are structured codes and amounts; the existing rules service handles the complete decision with a measured 40 ms p95.
additions.decisiveConstraint: There is no language ambiguity or missing evidence for Claude to resolve, and the current deterministic path already meets the SLA.
additions.expectedDecision: Do not introduce Claude; keep the rules service as the production solution and reserve Claude for a separate unstructured explanation or support need if one is evidenced.
additions.rationale: Correct business-to-solution framing can reject an LLM when the job is fully structured and a simpler system already satisfies the outcome.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Add a Claude classification call because the volume is large and the business wants an AI solution.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: It adds cost and probabilistic failure without solving a language problem or improving the measured latency and decision contract.
additions.counterfactual: If exception descriptions became free-form and the rules service could not parse them, Claude could extract structured facts before the same rules decision.
additions.sourceSection: When (and when not) to use agents
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends the simplest solution that meets the need and notes that added agentic complexity trades latency and cost for performance; the no-LLM conclusion follows from this scenario’s fully deterministic task.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered business-to-solution decision: decline an LLM when all inputs and rules are structured and the deterministic path already meets the SLA; this is distinct from authority-boundary scenarios.

additions.scenario: A warehouse dashboard must raise alerts within 100 ms p95 from structured event codes, while incident commanders want a post-incident narrative assembled from free-form logs, notes, and chat.
additions.evidence: Rules aggregation meets the 100 ms p95 alert SLA; a pilot Claude narrative over an incident packet cut handoff preparation 35% on reviewed cases, but the model call adds about 600 ms.
additions.decisiveConstraint: The alert path has a hard 100 ms boundary; the narrative can run asynchronously only over an immutable incident snapshot with an explicit freshness and source-version boundary.
additions.expectedDecision: Emit immediate deterministic alerts from event aggregation and enqueue an asynchronous Claude narrative over the versioned incident snapshot, exposing freshness and citations and requiring incident-commander review before distribution.
additions.rationale: This separates a deterministic safety-critical path from a measured Claude use whose unstructured evidence creates business value after the alert; it does not force one latency profile onto both outcomes.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Call Claude synchronously for every alert and truncate the incident evidence to recover latency.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: The measured call still violates the alert SLA, and truncation discards the free-form evidence that produced the narrative benefit.
additions.counterfactual: If a new benchmark showed Claude fitting the 100 ms p95 alert budget while preserving the required evidence freshness, a synchronous model path could be considered for that alert decision.
additions.sourceSection: When (and when not) to use agents
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends starting with the simplest solution and adding agentic complexity only when it is needed, because agentic systems trade latency and cost for task performance.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered transfer decision: split a hard-SLA deterministic alert from a measured asynchronous Claude narrative over versioned unstructured evidence; the model has a real business role without entering the alert critical path.

additions.scenario: A billing service receives free-form technician notes alongside normalized codes. The deterministic posting rules meet their latency target for coded records, but the notes contain the only description of an unclassified fault.
additions.evidence: Two hundred thousand records arrive daily; 3% contain free-form notes; held-out notes can be labeled; the rules service already validates and posts normalized fields.
additions.decisiveConstraint: Language ambiguity exists only in the note field, while the deterministic service must retain authority for final posting.
additions.expectedDecision: Use Claude to extract candidate structured facts from the notes with evidence and an explicit uncertainty state, then send them through the existing deterministic validation and posting path.
additions.rationale: The business need now includes an evidenced unstructured extraction step, so a narrowly augmented model adds value without replacing the proven decision service.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Keep the rules-only path and reject every note-bearing record for manual entry.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: It preserves deterministic authority but leaves the measured unstructured bottleneck unsolved even though a bounded extraction experiment is available.
additions.counterfactual: If the notes were removed or fully normalized before arrival, retain the rules-only design from CCARP-D01-O01-scenario-01.
additions.sourceSection: When (and when not) to use agents
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends starting with the simplest solution and adding agentic complexity only when it is needed, because agentic systems trade latency and cost for task performance.
additions.auditFinding: Adds the positive counterpart to the existing deterministic no-LLM case: use a bounded extraction step only when free-form evidence creates a measured language task.
additions.contrastBeforeDecision: The existing paired item keeps Claude out because inputs, rules, and the measured SLA are fully deterministic.
additions.contrastAfterDecision: This item introduces a measured free-text fault bottleneck, so Claude extraction becomes useful before the same rules boundary.

additions.scenario: A clinic referral desk processes 3,000 forms each week. Staff work from a queue, never from chat; they correct missing fields before scheduling. A summarizer pilot cuts first review from 6.0 to 4.5 minutes but raises correction rate from 4% to 9%.
additions.evidence: The only feasible user surface is an asynchronous queue item with structured fields and a missing-data state. Leadership counts completed appointments and total handling time, including corrections.
additions.decisiveConstraint: Translate the request into a queue-based intake workflow and keep expansion gated on end-to-end handling and appointment outcomes, not on shorter first review alone.
additions.expectedDecision: Build a structured referral extractor that flags missing fields for staff, keeps scheduling authority with the desk, and expand only if total handling time and completed-appointment quality improve against baseline.
additions.rationale: The decision fits the actual work surface and prevents a local summarization gain from being mistaken for business value.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Launch a conversational assistant because the first-review time improved and let staff adapt their workflow around it.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: Chat is unavailable in the operating process, and the higher correction rate means the local gain may increase total work rather than improve the business outcome.
additions.counterfactual: If correction rate returned to baseline and total handling time fell while completed-appointment quality held, expansion of the queue workflow would be justified.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends clear success criteria and empirical tests before prompt improvement, making the business objective testable.
additions.auditFinding: Adds an operating-surface decision: a queue contract with missingness and staff ownership is required before measuring value; this is not a clinic rename of the existing outage workflow.
additions.integrationConstraint: D1.6 requires total handling time and completed appointments to decide expansion; if only first-review time is measured, the expected decision changes from a bounded queue pilot to no expansion.

objectiveLabel: Design end-to-end architectures (input → processing → output → feedback loops)

existing.scenario: An insurer needs claim text validated, enriched with policy context, assigned to a queue, reviewed by an adjuster, and evaluated from production outcomes.
existing.evidence: Queue assignment is advisory; adjuster decisions are available for labels.
existing.decisiveConstraint: The architecture must preserve each input, processing, output, and real-world feedback stage.
existing.expectedDecision: Use normalized input, retrieval, structured assignment, adjuster correction, and labeled evaluation records.
existing.rationale: The downstream decision is the meaningful signal; model confidence or retrieval similarity cannot replace it.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Send raw narratives to Claude and display prose without storing assignments or outcomes.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: It cannot trace failures or learn from whether adjusters accepted the recommendation.
existing.counterfactual: If the assignment were never reviewed and no external outcome existed, the proposed feedback loop would need an explicit proxy or labeled test process.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic says agents need ground truth from the environment at each step and recommends stopping conditions and human feedback checkpoints.
existing.auditFinding: The end-to-end chain is valid, but option c is strictly longest; rewrite all choices to comparable stage coverage and make the feedback distinction less obvious by length.

existing.scenario: A contract review service logs JSON output but cannot connect missed renewal clauses to document versions or lawyer outcomes.
existing.evidence: Generated text exists; the review application already has lawyer accept, edit, and reject decisions.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Diagnose failures by input version and reviewer ground truth before changing the model.
existing.expectedDecision: Persist document and policy versions, reviewer outcome, corrected value, and links to evaluation cases.
existing.rationale: Versioned outcome traces expose the slice that failed and make a repair testable.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Increase output tokens or add a paraphrasing model.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: More prose does not identify the failed input or whether the lawyer considered it correct.
existing.counterfactual: If lawyer decisions were unavailable, the team would need an independent labeled evaluation set before diagnosing the production miss.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic emphasizes environmental ground truth and human feedback checkpoints for assessing agent progress.
existing.auditFinding: The diagnosis is useful, but option a is strictly longest and the same versioned reviewer-evidence recipe is repeated by the boundary slot; rewrite options and reserve this row for failure attribution.

existing.scenario: A contract pipeline stores only the final renewal recommendation and discards the lawyer's override and document provenance.
existing.evidence: The lawyer is operational ground truth; investigation requires input and revision linkage.
existing.decisiveConstraint: The row repeats the diagnosis slot's versioned input plus reviewer outcome decision.
existing.expectedDecision: Merge this coverage into `CCARP-D01-O02-diagnosis` and retire the duplicate slot as a separate learning decision.
existing.rationale: Both items ask for the same durable trace and differ only in wording and field granularity; keeping both inflates breadth without a new decision.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Keep aggregate acceptance percentages or trust the generated recommendation.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Aggregates and self-accepted outputs cannot localize a failure or preserve corrected evidence.
existing.counterfactual: If the boundary instead tested an external side effect with timeout and idempotency, it would be a distinct end-to-end decision and should remain separate.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic says agents need ground truth from the environment and can pause for human feedback at checkpoints.
existing.auditFinding: Clear semantic duplicate of the diagnosis row; merge rather than count another question. The accepted option is also strictly longest.

existing.scenario: A fraud workflow may place an account hold, but a network timeout can leave the external operation's result unknown.
existing.evidence: The operation is retryable; operations needs eventual status.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Recovery must use durable external state, checkpoints, and bounded retries rather than model memory.
existing.expectedDecision: Persist hold status, checkpoint after confirmed feedback, and apply finite retry/recovery policy.
existing.rationale: This is a distinct end-to-end reliability decision about delayed side-effect state, not merely reviewer labeling.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Let Claude remember whether it applied the hold and retry indefinitely.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Model memory is not a source of truth and unlimited retries can compound side effects.
existing.counterfactual: If the operation were read-only and idempotent with a synchronous result, durable hold state and recovery checkpoints would not be the first boundary.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic describes durable execution with resumable state and deterministic safeguards such as retry logic and regular checkpoints for long-running agents.
existing.auditFinding: Controller inspected every canonical option: preserve the useful scenario and decision, but replace implausible distractors that advertise unsafe, unmeasured, untyped, arbitrary, or explicitly unverified behavior; provide professional competing actions that lose on the stated constraint and align per-option feedback.

additions.scenario: A payment assistant creates a refund request, but the billing API may return a timeout after committing the refund.
additions.evidence: Refunds have a request ID and status endpoint; duplicate refunds are financially material.
additions.decisiveConstraint: The system must distinguish unknown, committed, and failed states before retrying a side effect.
additions.expectedDecision: Send an idempotency key, persist request state, poll the authoritative status, and route unresolved cases to operations instead of blindly retrying.
additions.rationale: The end-to-end architecture needs a durable handoff between model proposal and external mutation, with replay behavior defined at the service boundary.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Retry the same refund call until the API returns success.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: A timeout can follow a committed mutation, so repeated calls may issue duplicate refunds.
additions.counterfactual: If the billing API guaranteed idempotency for the same request key and exposed durable status, a retry could be automated after checking that contract.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic describes durable execution with resumable state, retry logic, and checkpoints for long-running agents; the idempotency key and authoritative refund-status semantics here come from the stated billing API contract.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered decision: bind a model-proposed side effect to an idempotent service contract and authoritative status before retry; this adds a mutation-specific boundary beyond the current hold example.

additions.scenario: A claims recommender is accepted by reviewers, but customer resolution occurs weeks later and is linked to several prompt and policy releases.
additions.evidence: The service can retain case, release, reviewer decision, and eventual resolution outcome IDs.
additions.decisiveConstraint: Feedback must join delayed business outcomes to the exact versioned path that produced the recommendation.
additions.expectedDecision: Record an asynchronous outcome event and correlate it with input, model/prompt/policy versions, review action, and later resolution.
additions.rationale: Immediate acceptance is a useful checkpoint but not the final business ground truth; delayed outcomes enable cohort diagnosis and safe iteration.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Treat reviewer acceptance as the complete success signal and overwrite old release attribution.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: Acceptance can coexist with later failure, and overwritten provenance prevents identifying which release caused the outcome.
additions.counterfactual: If the recommendation had no downstream outcome beyond immediate human acceptance, the shorter reviewer checkpoint could be the valid endpoint.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic emphasizes environmental ground truth and human feedback checkpoints for assessing agent progress.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered decision: model delayed outcome events as first-class feedback and preserve release attribution; it differs from immediate accept/edit/reject capture.

additions.scenario: A document intake service extracts fields for an ERP import; malformed JSON and missing required fields must not reach the posting step.
additions.evidence: The ERP has a typed schema and a quarantine queue; reviewers can inspect rejected documents.
additions.decisiveConstraint: The generated output becomes an operational record only after deterministic validation and explicit failure routing.
additions.expectedDecision: Validate schema and business constraints, quarantine invalid results with source and version, and release only conforming records.
additions.rationale: The output contract is an end-to-end boundary between probabilistic extraction and a deterministic downstream system.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Parse whatever fields are present and let the ERP reject malformed records later.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: Deferred rejection loses clear ownership, contaminates downstream state, and weakens retry and diagnosis evidence.
additions.counterfactual: If the downstream system accepted an immutable draft rather than posting state, validation could be advisory before human review.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic's agent guidance emphasizes environmental ground truth, stopping conditions, and human checkpoints; schema and business validation, quarantine, and ERP release are application controls supplied by the stated downstream contract.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered decision: place deterministic schema and business validation at the point where Claude output crosses into an ERP record; this differs from feedback capture and side-effect timeout recovery.

additions.scenario: A billing gateway returns an explicit REJECTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH for a refund request. No provider request ID exists, the gateway contract guarantees the provider was not called, and the user token, approval, and spend budget are still valid.
additions.evidence: The existing refund service supports an idempotency key and distinguishes a proven pre-dispatch rejection from an unknown outcome. A retry is bounded to one attempt.
additions.decisiveConstraint: A proven pre-dispatch rejection permits a bounded safe retry after current authorization checks; an unknown side-effect state still requires authoritative reconciliation.
additions.expectedDecision: Persist the rejection event, revalidate subject, approval, scope, and budget, retry once with the same idempotency key, and route any subsequent unknown result to status reconciliation.
additions.rationale: The service proof changes the side-effect state from unknown to not dispatched, so recovery can progress without blind repetition.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Treat every failure as an unknown side effect and wait for reconciliation before attempting any retry.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: That discards the gateway contract that proves no provider call occurred and can leave a valid refund unnecessarily unresolved.
additions.counterfactual: If the gateway could not prove pre-dispatch rejection or returned a provider request ID, keep the existing poll-and-reconcile decision and do not retry blindly.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic says agents need ground truth from the environment at each step and recommends stopping conditions and human feedback checkpoints.
additions.auditFinding: True reversal of the existing unknown-side-effect refund row: explicit service evidence permits a bounded retry, whereas uncertainty requires status lookup.
additions.contrastBeforeDecision: The existing paired item has an uncertain provider state, so its decision is reconciliation before retry.
additions.contrastAfterDecision: This item has a contract-level proof that dispatch never occurred, so the decision becomes a bounded retry after revalidation.

additions.scenario: An account-closure assistant may prepare a closure request. Closure is irreversible, identity and retention checks are deterministic, and a compliance officer must confirm the evidence immediately before execution.
additions.evidence: The assistant can assemble the request and citations; the closure service exposes a status operation and records the authorizing officer.
additions.decisiveConstraint: The model may prepare work, but authorization and the final external mutation require a current deterministic check and human checkpoint.
additions.expectedDecision: Persist the request and evidence, run identity and retention checks, obtain the officer confirmation at the checkpoint, execute once through the closure service, and record the result.
additions.rationale: The stages give the model a useful preparation role while making the consequential action, approval, and outcome observable and replayable.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Let Claude close the account after it cites the retention policy, then notify compliance in the audit report.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: A citation does not prove current authorization and post-action notification cannot prevent an irreversible closure.
additions.counterfactual: If closure were reversible and explicitly delegated to the service account, the human checkpoint could be replaced by a measured automated approval policy.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic says agents need ground truth from the environment and can pause for human feedback at checkpoints.
additions.auditFinding: Adds a concrete end-to-end side-effect gate integrating authorization and observability into the checkpoint decision.
additions.integrationConstraint: D3.2 requires a current subject and scope check at invocation; D3.4 requires parent, approval, and service-outcome links. If authorization is revoked or lineage is absent, the expected decision changes from execution to explicit stop and reauthorization/audit repair.

objectiveLabel: Select appropriate architectural patterns (workflow, agentic, augmented LLM)

existing.scenario: Article drafting has known subtasks and order, including a fixed style gate.
existing.evidence: The sequence is predictable and each stage can be checked programmatically.
existing.decisiveConstraint: No dynamic planning or subtask discovery is required.
existing.expectedDecision: Use a prompt-chaining workflow with outline, draft, style check, and final output stages.
existing.rationale: A fixed workflow exposes stage boundaries and keeps the programmatic gate explicit.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Use an autonomous agent to choose the article stages on every request.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: It adds planning variability where the path is already known and inspectable.
existing.counterfactual: If the number and order of research or drafting steps changed with discoveries, an agentic loop would be better aligned.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic defines prompt chaining as sequential LLM calls and recommends it when a task can be cleanly decomposed into fixed subtasks.
existing.auditFinding: The pattern is correct, but the accepted option is tied for shortest/near-shortest while the distractors remain uneven; rewrite options with comparable stage detail and comparable action scope.

existing.scenario: Market research has an unpredictable number of searches and follow-up paths, with discoveries changing the next action.
existing.evidence: The task is open-ended and path-dependent; search results are available to guide the next step.
existing.decisiveConstraint: The architecture must plan and use tools iteratively with explicit stop limits.
existing.expectedDecision: Use an agentic loop that plans, searches, evaluates evidence, and stops on completion or bounded limits.
existing.rationale: The next useful action cannot be specified as a fixed chain before evidence arrives.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Use a static three-search prompt chain for every investigation.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: A fixed search count cannot adapt when evidence creates a new necessary line of inquiry.
existing.counterfactual: If the source set and search sequence were fixed and fully known, prompt chaining would reduce variability and cost.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic says agents fit open-ended problems whose number of steps cannot be predicted and describes them as LLMs using tools in a loop.
existing.auditFinding: The agent diagnosis is sound, but option d is strictly longest and telegraphs the key; rebalance alternatives while keeping the unpredictable-step evidence decisive.

existing.scenario: Technicians ask grounded questions about a 60-page maintenance handbook; the handbook fits context and no external action is needed.
existing.evidence: The answer must cite the handbook; there is no need for planning or tool side effects.
existing.decisiveConstraint: A single augmented response with source context is sufficient.
existing.expectedDecision: Use an augmented LLM with supplied or retrieved handbook context and citations.
existing.rationale: Retrieval and source context add knowledge without adding an unnecessary agent loop.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Use an exploratory agent with a handbook retrieval tool for every question.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Dynamic exploration adds latency and coordination without an open-ended action requirement.
existing.counterfactual: If troubleshooting required iterative tool checks or changing hypotheses, an agentic pattern could earn its added complexity.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic describes retrieval, tools, and memory as augmentations to an LLM and advises adding complexity only when simpler solutions fall short.

existing.scenario: Support messages map to three stable categories and API/policy paths, while ambiguous classification must reach a human.
existing.evidence: Categories and downstream actions are known; uncertainty is observable.
existing.decisiveConstraint: The system must route to specialized paths and preserve an explicit ambiguity route.
existing.expectedDecision: Classify first, route to category-specific workflow, and hand low-confidence cases to a human.
existing.rationale: Routing separates stable concerns and prevents uncertain input from silently crossing a policy boundary.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Apply one general support workflow and shared policy/API surface to every category, then send exceptions to a human after the workflow has attempted the request.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: A shared path does not enforce the distinct category policy and API contract before a side effect; deferring ambiguity to a post-action exception can send a sensitive or invalid request to the wrong route.
existing.counterfactual: If categories or tools were unknown and discoveries changed the next step, an agentic pattern would replace the fixed router.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic describes routing as classifying an input and directing it to a specialized follow-up task, with separation of concerns.
existing.auditFinding: Exam-preparation audit: replaced message-length routing distractor with a plausible shared workflow whose post-action exception handling violates pre-action category and ambiguity boundaries.

additions.scenario: A service desk has an 80% FAQ workload and a 20% investigation workload requiring changing searches and evidence review.
additions.evidence: FAQ answers cite a stable knowledge base; investigations need tools and a bounded human escalation path.
additions.decisiveConstraint: One pattern must not force either simple requests into an agent loop or complex requests into a static answer.
additions.expectedDecision: Route FAQ requests to an augmented LLM path and investigative requests to a bounded agentic path, with evaluated thresholds.
additions.rationale: The heterogeneous workload requires composition: the pattern decision follows the task topology rather than a single global architecture.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Use one autonomous agent for every ticket so it can handle both categories.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: Routine requests pay unnecessary latency and tool-selection risk, while the architecture lacks a clear simple-path baseline.
additions.counterfactual: If all tickets followed the same fixed retrieval-and-answer path, routing and agentic exploration would add no justified value.
additions.sourceSection: When (and when not) to use agents
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic says agentic systems trade latency and cost for task performance and recommends increasing complexity only when it makes sense for the use case.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered pattern-composition decision: route distinct workload segments to the least complex sufficient pattern; this is separate from the other addition's fixed workflow with an agentic exception branch inside one case.

additions.scenario: A compliance report has fixed intake, extraction, and schema validation, followed by an open-ended evidence search only when an exception is detected.
additions.evidence: Most cases follow a known sequence; exception investigations require adaptive searches and a compliance owner signs the report.
additions.decisiveConstraint: The predictable path should stay controlled, while dynamic exploration is isolated to the exception branch.
additions.expectedDecision: Use a workflow for intake and validation, invoking a bounded agentic subpath only for exceptions before owner review.
additions.rationale: A hybrid boundary prevents the rare open-ended step from making every routine case autonomous and unbounded.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Make the complete report an unrestricted agent task from the first input.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: It adds planning and cost to fixed stages and makes the normal compliance path harder to validate.
additions.counterfactual: If exception search were never needed or every case required novel investigation, the hybrid split would collapse to a workflow or agent respectively.
additions.sourceSection: When (and when not) to use agents
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic says agents fit open-ended, unpredictable steps and recommends adding agentic complexity only when it makes sense for the use case; the fixed intake and validation stages remain a scenario-defined workflow.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered boundary decision: retain a workflow for every predictable stage and invoke bounded agentic exploration only on a detected exception branch; distinct from routing separate FAQ and investigation workloads.

additions.scenario: Technicians ask a maintenance question from a handbook and may then inspect live equipment, select among read tools based on readings, stop at a safety threshold, and request approval before a repair action.
additions.evidence: The handbook answer alone is bounded, but the next tool and number of checks depend on live readings; the repair service requires approval.
additions.decisiveConstraint: The action path has evidence-dependent steps and a consequential approval boundary, unlike a one-shot cited handbook answer.
additions.expectedDecision: Use a bounded agentic loop for read-only inspection with explicit stop conditions, then pass the proposed repair and evidence through deterministic checks and human approval before action.
additions.rationale: The required pattern changes when the system must choose follow-up tools from new evidence; the action boundary remains outside unrestricted model control.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Use the augmented LLM handbook path and ask the technician to infer the live reading and next action from the answer.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: Static handbook context cannot execute or adapt to live evidence, and inference from absent readings can produce an unsafe repair recommendation.
additions.counterfactual: If every answer came only from the handbook and no live tool or action were needed, retain the augmented LLM boundary in CCARP-D01-O03-boundary.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic says agents fit open-ended problems whose number of steps cannot be predicted and describes them as LLMs using tools in a loop.
additions.auditFinding: Adds an explicit pattern reversal against the current augmented-LLM item by introducing live evidence-dependent tool steps and a bounded action gate.
additions.contrastBeforeDecision: The existing paired item has a supplied handbook answer and no live tool loop, so an augmented LLM is proportionate.
additions.contrastAfterDecision: This item has reading-dependent steps and a safety stop, so an agentic inspection loop is required.

additions.scenario: A product-support workflow first performs an exact SKU and warranty-status lookup. For 94% of requests it returns a grounded answer in 220 ms p95 under a 500 ms synchronous SLA; for 6% it returns no active match or conflicting records. A research pilot improves accepted resolution on that evidence-gap slice from 61% to 79% but costs five times as much.
additions.evidence: The exact lookup is deterministic and cheap. A no-match or conflict can be queued for two searches over approved field notes under a separate three-minute asynchronous SLA; the user receives an explicit pending state and a human route if evidence remains unresolved.
additions.decisiveConstraint: Keep the 500 ms synchronous contract for routine exact lookups and defer the expensive research branch to an explicit asynchronous path only after the lookup proves an evidence gap.
additions.expectedDecision: Run the exact structured lookup synchronously, return its grounded result when it succeeds, and enqueue a bounded agentic research job only on a no-match or conflict state; expose pending, completion, citations, cost, and the three-minute timeout rather than running research inline.
additions.rationale: The routing decision is between a fast synchronous first stage and a deferred evidence-gap job with its own SLA, not a generic choice to make every hard request agentic.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Classify the user message as routine or investigative before lookup and run the research loop inline for messages that appear complex.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: The evidence gap is known only after the exact lookup, and inline research would violate the routine 500 ms contract when the catalog can resolve the request.
additions.counterfactual: If the exact lookup never produced a no-match or conflict, remove the asynchronous research job; if the business accepted one three-minute response for every request, re-evaluate the synchronous routing boundary.
additions.sourceClaim: Just-in-time retrieval uses lightweight identifiers to load detailed information only when relevant, keeping context focused.
additions.auditFinding: Adds a distinct conditional routing architecture: synchronous exact lookup for the routine slice and a separately budgeted asynchronous agentic job only after a proven evidence gap; it is not generic workload-category routing.
additions.integrationConstraint: D3.6 requires exact structured lookup before semantic or exploratory retrieval; changing the deferred branch to inline semantic search would break the 500 ms routine SLA, while a failed lookup is the condition that changes the retrieval path.

objectiveLabel: Design multi-agent systems and orchestration strategies

existing.scenario: Twelve independent industry investigations can run concurrently, but a lead must reconcile one report.
existing.evidence: Workers need separate source paths; synthesis and citation reconciliation remain centralized.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Parallel exploration must return bounded reports to one synthesis owner.
existing.expectedDecision: Use an orchestrator-worker design with focused parallel workers and a lead synthesis contract.
existing.rationale: The topology has independent breadth followed by a dependent integration step.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Publish twelve independent reports directly to the customer.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Without a synthesis owner, overlap, contradictions, and missing cross-cutting conclusions remain unresolved.
existing.counterfactual: If every investigation shared mutable state or depended on the previous industry result, parallel workers would no longer be the right topology.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic describes a lead orchestrator that delegates specialized research to parallel subagents and synthesizes their findings.
existing.auditFinding: The topology is sound, but option c is strictly longest; rewrite alternatives to expose comparable orchestration details and preserve a credible parallelism trade-off.

existing.scenario: Four migration agents receive shared repository history and edit dependent files concurrently, causing conflicts and reconciliation overhead.
existing.evidence: Subtasks share state and have many dependencies; concurrent edits overwrite assumptions.
existing.decisiveConstraint: The design must preserve one authoritative state across dependent transformations.
existing.expectedDecision: Use a coordinated single agent or sequential workflow with explicit checkpoints.
existing.rationale: Multi-agent parallelism is a poor fit when workers require the same context and outputs are tightly dependent.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Add more agents and let the last writer win.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: More workers multiply conflicts and last-writer-wins can silently discard correct work.
existing.counterfactual: If each migration unit had isolated files and no cross-unit dependencies, bounded parallel workers could improve throughput.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic notes that multi-agent systems are a poor fit when agents must share the same context or when many dependencies exist between agents.
existing.auditFinding: The diagnosis is valid, but option a is strictly longest by a wide margin; rewrite the options so the dependency evidence, not answer length, identifies the fit.

existing.scenario: Labor, tax, and environmental specialists research separate rule sets and return evidence; only a lead may issue the customer-facing conclusion.
existing.evidence: Each worker has a distinct source area; the lead needs claims, locations, uncertainty, and conflict visibility.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Worker outputs must be bounded evidence artifacts, not final authority.
existing.expectedDecision: Define worker objectives, source/tool guidance, output format, and no-conclusion boundary; lead validates and synthesizes.
existing.rationale: Explicit contracts reduce duplicated research and prevent authority from drifting to specialists.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Give every specialist the same broad goal and allow each to publish an answer.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Vague ownership encourages overlap and permits specialists to cross the customer-facing authority boundary.
existing.counterfactual: If specialists owned independent customer decisions with no synthesis, a lead-only conclusion boundary would not be required.
existing.sourceSection: Prompt engineering and evaluations for research agents
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic found that workers need an objective, output format, tool and source guidance, and clear task boundaries to avoid duplicated work and gaps.
existing.auditFinding: The worker contract is correct, but option d is strictly longest and signals the answer; rewrite choices with comparable contract specificity.

existing.scenario: One hundred independent invoices can be processed concurrently; each extracted result must pass deterministic schema and business validation before posting.
existing.evidence: Invoice tasks have no dependencies; malformed results can be quarantined.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Use bounded fan-out while preserving per-item validation and failure isolation.
existing.expectedDecision: Fan out focused workers with bounded concurrency and validate each result before acceptance.
existing.rationale: It exploits independence without giving workers unvalidated side effects.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Let workers post invoices directly to avoid a lead bottleneck.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Direct posting bypasses the required validation boundary and makes a worker responsible for unnecessary state changes.
existing.counterfactual: If invoices had cross-record dependencies or required a shared mutable ledger, independent fan-out would need a different coordination design.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic describes sectioning independent subtasks in parallel and aggregating their outputs programmatically.
existing.auditFinding: Controller inspected every canonical option: preserve the useful scenario and decision, but replace implausible distractors that advertise unsafe, unmeasured, untyped, arbitrary, or explicitly unverified behavior; provide professional competing actions that lose on the stated constraint and align per-option feedback.

additions.scenario: A global diligence project first splits work by market, then each market requires separate legal, pricing, and competitor investigations before one lead report.
additions.evidence: Market work is independent; each market's subquestions are also independent but share a local evidence contract.
additions.decisiveConstraint: The system needs hierarchical ownership without passing every raw search transcript to the top-level lead.
additions.expectedDecision: Use hierarchical orchestrator-workers: a lead assigns markets, market workers delegate bounded subquestions, and structured reports roll up through validation.
additions.rationale: A flat pool loses market-level ownership, while a single context loses focus; hierarchical delegation matches two independent levels of breadth.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Have one lead agent search every market and subquestion sequentially.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: It creates a context and latency bottleneck and makes it difficult to attribute missing evidence to a market or subquestion.
additions.counterfactual: If every subquestion depended on one shared evolving hypothesis, hierarchical parallelism would create stale assumptions and should be reduced.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic describes a lead orchestrator delegating specialized research to parallel subagents and synthesizing findings; applying that ownership contract recursively to independent market subquestions is the scenario's architectural deduction.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered orchestration decision: preserve ownership at two aggregation levels when a broad task has independent nested work; distinct from the existing flat fan-out examples.

additions.scenario: Three research workers return conflicting revenue figures from different dated filings; the lead must publish one figure with an evidence trail.
additions.evidence: Each worker records source location and date; conflict can be resolved by a targeted verification task.
additions.decisiveConstraint: Aggregation must detect disagreement and preserve provenance instead of choosing by majority or fluent synthesis.
additions.expectedDecision: Run a conflict detector, request focused verification of the disputed claim, and make the lead resolve or expose the uncertainty.
additions.rationale: Independent parallel results need an explicit arbitration path when evidence conflicts; synthesis alone is not a correctness guarantee.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Ask the lead to choose the number cited by the most workers.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: Repeated claims can share a copied source or stale date, so count is weaker than verified provenance.
additions.counterfactual: If all workers used one authoritative synchronized record and conflicts were impossible by contract, a separate arbitration step would be unnecessary.
additions.sourceSection: Prompt engineering and evaluations for research agents
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic requires worker objectives, output formats, source and tool guidance, and clear boundaries; conflict detection, focused verification, and uncertainty publication are the scenario's application-level aggregation policy.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered decision: make conflicts a first-class aggregate state and route only disputed claims to verification; this differs from simple completeness gating.

additions.scenario: Twelve analysts investigate one shared market model. Each analyst needs the full evolving context, and the next analyst's task depends on the previous analyst's interpretation; a lead still owns the final brief.
additions.evidence: Workers repeatedly edit shared assumptions, and prior parallel runs produced contradictory state and reconciliation work.
additions.decisiveConstraint: The workers share context and have many dependencies, so independent parallel agents would not create isolated throughput.
additions.expectedDecision: Use one coordinated context with staged handoffs or a small dependency-aware workflow, preserving a lead checkpoint rather than fanning out twelve independent agents.
additions.rationale: Multi-agent parallelism is a poor fit when workers must share the same context and many dependencies; coordination should follow the actual topology.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Run twelve parallel specialists with full shared context and ask the lead to reconcile all differences at the end.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: Shared context and dependent edits create conflicts before synthesis, so a final reconciliation cannot recover reliable ownership or ordering.
additions.counterfactual: If each market had independent evidence and no worker depended on another's state, use the parallel specialist design from CCARP-D01-O04-selection.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic notes that multi-agent systems are a poor fit when agents must share the same context or when many dependencies exist between agents.
additions.auditFinding: Adds the documented negative boundary for multi-agent systems and flips the current independent-specialist choice using shared context and dependent state.
additions.contrastBeforeDecision: The existing item has independent specialist reports that can be scoped and synthesized.
additions.contrastAfterDecision: This item requires the same evolving context and dependent interpretations, so parallel specialists are a poor fit.

additions.scenario: A lead coordinates six jurisdiction specialists in parallel. Each worker has a separate OAuth scope; five return complete evidence packets, while one worker retrieves its packet and then loses its scope before synthesis. Organization policy requires access to remain valid at aggregation for every mandatory region.
additions.evidence: The lead can verify worker identity, current scope, source jurisdiction, completion status, and parent run ID. The policy forbids publishing a complete cross-jurisdiction conclusion without the mandatory region; an explicit unavailable region is allowed only when the policy marks that region optional.
additions.decisiveConstraint: Parallelism remains useful, but the organization policy makes current authorization at aggregation an admissibility gate; retrieved data is not automatically invalidated by OAuth revocation, yet it cannot be published for a mandatory region without a current policy-approved access decision.
additions.expectedDecision: Run bounded scoped workers in parallel, revalidate current scope and policy at aggregation, quarantine the revoked worker packet, and reauthorize or retry it before synthesis. Do not publish the complete comparison; publish an explicit unavailable region only if the governing policy permits that region to be optional.
additions.rationale: The topology stays parallel while the organization policy, rather than revocation alone, determines whether an already retrieved packet may enter the lead’s synthesis.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Accept the five returned packets because the revoked worker already retrieved its evidence, and infer the mandatory jurisdiction from neighboring reports.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: The organization policy requires valid access at aggregation for the mandatory region, and neighboring evidence is not authority for that jurisdiction; inferred coverage would falsely claim completeness.
additions.counterfactual: If current scope remains valid at aggregation, accept the packet after the same source and completeness checks. If policy explicitly designates the region optional, publish the other regions with that region marked unavailable.
additions.sourceSection: Prompt engineering and evaluations for research agents
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic found that workers need an objective, output format, tool and source guidance, and clear task boundaries to avoid duplicated work and gaps.
additions.auditFinding: Adds an authorization-policy aggregation boundary distinct from incident conflict follow-up and generic partial-worker retry; it makes the admissibility rule explicit.
additions.integrationConstraint: D3.2 requires current scope, tenant/jurisdiction binding, and organization-policy evaluation at aggregation; if policy permits an optional unavailable region, the decision changes to an explicitly partial report, but revocation alone does not justify treating retrieved evidence as erased.

objectiveLabel: Apply decomposition techniques for complex problem solving

existing.scenario: Eighty endpoint mappings share one terminology table, then can run independently before a compatibility gate.
existing.evidence: Terminology is a prerequisite; every mapping must be checked before guide assembly.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Materialize the shared artifact first, then parallelize independent partitions and gate completeness.
existing.expectedDecision: Create and approve terminology, fan out mappings that consume it, and aggregate through a compatibility gate.
existing.rationale: The split follows the real dependency boundary and preserves artifacts for verification.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Fan out immediately and let each worker define terminology locally.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Local definitions drift and concatenation provides no reliable consistency check.
existing.counterfactual: If mappings were coupled through shared evolving state, independent fan-out would need a sequential or coordinated plan.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic describes parallelization as running independent subtasks concurrently and aggregating their outputs programmatically.
existing.auditFinding: The dependency split is sound, but option b is strictly longest; rebalance options while keeping shared artifact, fan-out, and gate as the decisive sequence.

existing.scenario: One security prompt misses one of three independent risk dimensions; all findings must feed a release recommendation.
existing.evidence: Authentication, data exposure, and dependency checks use separate rubrics and need complete evidence.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Decompose by independent mental units and verify that every unit contributes before aggregation.
existing.expectedDecision: Run focused checks in parallel and combine them through a completeness gate.
existing.rationale: Separate attention and an explicit gate address omission better than repetition or a longer prompt.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Repeat the same whole review three times and choose the longest answer.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Repeated broad prompts can share the same blind spot and provide no coverage guarantee.
existing.counterfactual: If one risk dimension required another's raw reasoning, the units would need a dependency edge rather than parallel execution.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic reports that sectioning independent considerations into separate calls can improve focused performance, with outputs aggregated programmatically.
existing.auditFinding: The coverage diagnosis is valid, but option c is strictly longest; rewrite options with comparable evidence and a less obvious aggregation description.

existing.scenario: A repository migration has an unknown number of module-specific database and API changes revealed only by inspection.
existing.evidence: The task topology is input-dependent; a lead must synthesize a coherent plan after discovery.
existing.decisiveConstraint: The decomposition must be formed from repository evidence rather than a fixed task list.
existing.expectedDecision: Use an orchestrator to inspect, dynamically assign focused subtasks, and synthesize their artifacts.
existing.rationale: Dynamic decomposition is needed when both the number and nature of work units are unknown in advance.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Define one worker per module before inspecting the repository.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: It creates missing or irrelevant workers and assumes a topology the input cannot support.
existing.counterfactual: If modules and change classes were enumerated and independent before execution, a fixed fan-out plan would be simpler and safer.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic distinguishes orchestrator-workers by its ability to dynamically break down tasks when subtasks cannot be predicted in advance.
existing.auditFinding: The dynamic split is sound, but option d is strictly longest; rewrite alternatives so evidence-driven decomposition, not prose length, carries the key.

existing.scenario: Privacy, retention, and access checks are independent, yet all evidence is required before a release owner decides.
existing.evidence: Each control has its own rubric; a missing result blocks the recommendation.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Partition by independent control and aggregate with a completeness and ownership gate.
existing.expectedDecision: Run focused checks and send all evidence to the release owner for final decision.
existing.rationale: It preserves both independent attention and final authority.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Let a generalist produce one fluent summary or let the privacy reviewer suppress other checks.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Fluency does not prove coverage, and one reviewer cannot remove independent requirements without a dependency.
existing.counterfactual: If retention depended on a privacy classification produced first, the decomposition would sequence that prerequisite before retention analysis.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic describes sectioning independent subtasks in parallel and aggregating their outputs programmatically.
existing.auditFinding: Controller inspected every canonical option: preserve the useful scenario and decision, but replace implausible distractors that advertise unsafe, unmeasured, untyped, arbitrary, or explicitly unverified behavior; provide professional competing actions that lose on the stated constraint and align per-option feedback.

additions.scenario: A regulatory assessment has 400 controls; evidence collection for some controls depends on a shared asset inventory, while control tests within each layer are independent.
additions.evidence: The inventory must be current before tests run; each test returns an owner, evidence location, and status.
additions.decisiveConstraint: Schedule dependent layers in topological order and parallelize only the independent antichain within each layer.
additions.expectedDecision: Build the inventory first, fan out eligible control tests by layer, and aggregate results with dependency and completeness checks.
additions.rationale: A dependency graph prevents both premature checks and unnecessary serialization; decomposition follows prerequisite edges rather than equal-sized batches.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Run all 400 control prompts concurrently and let the aggregator infer which evidence was available in time.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: Dependent checks may use stale or missing inventory, and post-hoc inference cannot repair invalid evidence timing.
additions.counterfactual: If no control consumed another's artifact, one bounded parallel layer would be sufficient and the inventory stage would not gate execution.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends running independent subtasks in parallel and aggregating their outputs; prerequisite ordering here is an application of that rule to the stated dependency graph.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered decomposition decision: execute prerequisite layers before parallelizing independent work inside each layer; this is more specific than a single shared artifact or broad parallel sectioning.

additions.scenario: A support archive contains 2 million messages; every message needs a coarse topic label, but only safety-related clusters require detailed case synthesis.
additions.evidence: Topic labeling is independent per message; the synthesis budget is limited and safety clusters have a separate review owner.
additions.decisiveConstraint: The decomposition must filter before expensive synthesis and preserve the message-to-cluster evidence path.
additions.expectedDecision: Map messages to structured labels, reduce them into safety clusters, then synthesize only selected clusters with traceable membership.
additions.rationale: A map-filter-reduce plan aligns compute with business relevance and avoids asking one context to carry the full archive.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Ask one agent to read the full archive and summarize every topic with equal effort.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: It spends context and calls on low-value cases and provides no explicit filter that the safety owner can inspect.
additions.counterfactual: If every topic required the same deep synthesis, filtering would remove required evidence and the decomposition should use uniformly bounded partitions.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic says prompt chaining fits cleanly decomposed fixed subtasks; map, evidence-defined filtering, and selective synthesis are the scenario's application of that decomposition principle.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered decomposition decision: use a staged map-filter-reduce plan when an expensive subtask applies only to an evidence-defined subset; distinct from parallel completeness checks.

additions.scenario: A migration validates 10,000 independent records. Every record has all required schema fields, checks the same fixed rules, and returns the same result contract; no record depends on another record or a shared generated term list.
additions.evidence: A serial workflow takes 11 minutes; bounded fanout and programmatic aggregation complete in 90 seconds at the tested concurrency without changing the validation result.
additions.decisiveConstraint: With no prerequisite or cross-record dependency, independent checks should be decomposed for parallel execution rather than forced through a prerequisite stage.
additions.expectedDecision: Map records to independent validation tasks, run them with bounded concurrency, aggregate by record ID, and apply one completeness and error gate before release.
additions.rationale: The absence of dependencies makes parallel decomposition the simpler and faster choice while preserving a complete aggregate contract.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Create a shared terminology stage first, then fan out mappings that consume it as in a dependency-aware workflow.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: There is no shared artifact for the records to consume, so the added stage only serializes work and introduces an unnecessary failure point.
additions.counterfactual: If a generated schema or shared vocabulary became a prerequisite for every record, create that stage and run only the dependent checks afterward.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic describes parallelization as running independent subtasks concurrently and aggregating their outputs programmatically.
additions.auditFinding: True reversal of the existing prerequisite-first design: the new evidence removes the shared dependency, so independent map and aggregate is the correct strategy.
additions.contrastBeforeDecision: The existing paired item has a generated terminology artifact consumed by later mapping tasks.
additions.contrastAfterDecision: This item states that every record is independent and has no shared artifact, so prerequisite staging is counterproductive.

additions.scenario: A compliance audit has 1,200 controls. A deterministic precheck clears 1,080, while 120 failures cluster into eight causes. The request input budget is 16,000 tokens: current case evidence uses 10,000, and all four rare diagnostic tool schemas add 14,000, while the selected schema for one cause adds 3,000.
additions.evidence: Every cause needs one accountable evidence packet; a cause may be decomposed further only when its evidence is contradictory. Exposing all schemas would require 24,000 input tokens before output reserve, while exposing the selected schema keeps the request at 13,000 and leaves 3,000 tokens for the required reserve.
additions.decisiveConstraint: Decomposition must follow observed failure clusters and admit only the tool schema needed for the assigned cause so the 16,000-token budget and output reserve remain intact.
additions.expectedDecision: Run the precheck, assign one bounded owner per failing cause, use governed deferred tool discovery to expose only the selected 3,000-token schema for that cause, and spawn a further focused task only for a concrete contradiction before aggregating the eight packets.
additions.rationale: The numeric budget makes capability admission part of the decomposition boundary: the work is grouped by evidence and the tool surface is selected per group.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Create one agent and expose all four diagnostic schemas for every control so any failure can call any tool immediately.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: The eager surface adds 14,000 tokens to a 10,000-token case, exceeds the 16,000-token input budget before output reserve, and duplicates work for 1,080 controls already cleared.
additions.counterfactual: If the case evidence fell to 2,000 tokens or all four schemas became mandatory for one cause, recalculate admission; if the request still exceeds 16,000, queue or narrow it instead of evicting mandatory evidence.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends loading the most critical tools while deferring others for discovery when the tool inventory is large.
additions.auditFinding: Adds a concrete failure-cluster decomposition with 16,000-token admission arithmetic and an approved D3.1 deferred-tool mechanism; it is distinct from generic dynamic decomposition.
additions.integrationConstraint: D3.1 requires deferred tool selection to remain governed and authorized at invocation; if discovery cannot return the selected schema within the 16,000-token budget, the expected decision changes to a narrower or unavailable request rather than eager exposure.

objectiveLabel: Align solutions to business value pillars (efficiency, transformation, productivity, cost, performance SLAs)

existing.scenario: A retailer compares an efficient retrieval design at 1.8 seconds p95 and within budget with an agentic design at 6.4 seconds and over budget; staff can handle complex cases.
existing.evidence: High-volume routine traffic makes p95, unit cost, and routine quality material; handoff is available.
existing.decisiveConstraint: The selected design must meet measured cost and latency targets while verifying routine quality and edge-case routing.
existing.expectedDecision: Use the measured efficient candidate for routine cases, evaluate quality, and route uncertain cases to staff.
existing.rationale: It aligns the architecture to observed value pillars instead of treating capability as a proxy for business value.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Use the most capable agent for all requests and accept any unit cost.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: It violates the stated cost and p95 constraints and has no evidence that extra autonomy improves the target workload.
existing.counterfactual: If routine quality fell below the required floor or no staff handoff existed, the efficient design would not satisfy the service contract without another measured route.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends evaluating model capabilities, speed, cost, and effort against the actual use case rather than optimizing one dimension alone.
existing.auditFinding: The value decision is defensible, but option d is strictly longest; rewrite options with comparable measurement detail. Keep this row on business SLA alignment and operational routing; model-tier ownership belongs in D02-O01 only when model choice is the tested decision.

existing.scenario: A dashboard reports 92% conversation completion, but agents spend the same time because they rewrite many answers.
existing.evidence: Completion measures text returned; accepted work, resolution, edits, and time are observable.
existing.decisiveConstraint: The value signal must represent resolved customer work and the service SLA, not output production.
existing.expectedDecision: Measure resolution, accepted-answer rate, handling time, rework, and baseline comparison.
existing.rationale: The existing proxy rewards activity while masking unchanged productivity.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Raise the completion target or count longer answers as more productive.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Both preserve the mismatch between generated text and useful resolved work.
existing.counterfactual: If the business outcome were document generation volume with no review or resolution step, completion could be a valid leading measure, but that is not this workflow.
existing.sourceSection: Decide whether to upgrade or change models
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic advises testing with actual prompts and data and weighing performance and cost tradeoffs against use-case benchmarks.
existing.auditFinding: The metric diagnosis is sound, but option b is strictly longest; rewrite choices so outcome measures are not identifiable by length alone.

existing.scenario: A research group seeks potentially transformational discovery across a changing corpus; exploration is open-ended and researchers review cited findings.
existing.evidence: Discovery value may justify extra cost; evaluation, budgets, citations, and human review are available.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Agentic complexity must be justified by the transformation opportunity and bounded by measurable evidence and spend.
existing.expectedDecision: Pilot an evaluated agentic research path with stopping limits, citation requirements, cost tracking, and human review.
existing.rationale: The added flexibility earns its cost because the task's value depends on adaptive exploration.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Let the agent search indefinitely because transformation has no stopping point.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Unbounded execution converts exploratory value into uncontrolled cost and reliability risk.
existing.counterfactual: If the task were a fixed lookup with a strict low-latency budget, a bounded retrieval workflow would be the better value-aligned pattern.
existing.sourceSection: When (and when not) to use agents
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic says agentic systems trade latency and cost for task performance and recommends increasing complexity only when it makes sense for the use case.
existing.auditFinding: The cost-versus-transformation boundary is valid, but option c is strictly longest; rewrite all options with comparable evidence and explicit stopping behavior.

existing.scenario: A coding assistant generates many suggestions, but reviewers reject them and cleanup extends the engineering cycle.
existing.evidence: Accepted changes and end-to-end cycle time can be segmented and compared with the prior process.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Productivity means completed accepted work with less total cycle time, not suggestion volume.
existing.expectedDecision: Use accepted-change rate and end-to-end cycle time including review and rework as primary signals.
existing.rationale: The pair exposes downstream quality and process cost hidden by raw generation counts.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Count generated suggestions or output tokens as productivity.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: The observed rejection and rework show those activity measures are decoupled from productive work.
existing.counterfactual: If suggestions were auto-applied with independently verified tests and no review/rework stage, a generation measure could supplement but still not replace outcome evidence.
existing.sourceSection: Decide whether to upgrade or change models
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic advises testing with actual prompts and data and weighing performance and cost tradeoffs against use-case benchmarks.
existing.auditFinding: Controller inspected every canonical option: preserve the useful scenario and decision, but replace implausible distractors that advertise unsafe, unmeasured, untyped, arbitrary, or explicitly unverified behavior; provide professional competing actions that lose on the stated constraint and align per-option feedback.

additions.scenario: A contact center pilot cuts average handle time by 18% but lowers first-contact resolution from 84% to 72% and raises repeat contacts.
additions.evidence: The service target requires resolution at or above 82%; handle time, repeat contacts, and accepted answers are measured.
additions.decisiveConstraint: Efficiency cannot be accepted if it crosses the customer outcome floor; the SLA is a joint constraint.
additions.expectedDecision: Reject the current configuration for production, identify the resolution failure slice, and retest a bounded design that meets both handle-time and resolution thresholds.
additions.rationale: The decision aligns productivity with the actual service result and prevents one favorable metric from masking a material business regression.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Ship the pilot because an 18% handle-time reduction proves efficiency value.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: Lower resolution creates repeat work and violates the stated service outcome despite the average speed gain.
additions.counterfactual: If first-contact resolution stayed at or above 82% while handle time fell, the pilot could proceed to a broader adoption check.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends evaluating model capabilities, speed, cost, and effort against the actual use case rather than optimizing one dimension alone.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered value decision: treat a business outcome floor and efficiency target as joint acceptance criteria; distinct from measuring a proxy or selecting a model tier.

additions.scenario: An insurer proposes a Claude assistant as a transformation program, but the first release can only draft claim summaries for adjusters.
additions.evidence: The sponsor can measure adjuster adoption, time to decision, correction rate, and downstream claim outcomes; autonomous settlement is out of scope.
additions.decisiveConstraint: A transformation claim needs a staged value hypothesis linking adoption to a measurable business decision, not a grand feature label.
additions.expectedDecision: Define a narrow adjuster workflow, set adoption and time-to-decision leading measures plus claim-quality outcome measures, and gate expansion on evidence.
additions.rationale: It makes a broad transformation objective testable through a sequence of operational and business outcomes.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Declare transformation successful when the assistant is launched and users open its summary screen.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: Launch activity and screen views do not show faster, safer, or better claim decisions.
additions.counterfactual: If adjusters did not use the summaries or downstream claim outcomes could not be linked, the team should pause expansion and resolve measurement before calling the release transformational.
additions.sourceSection: Decide whether to upgrade or change models
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic advises testing with actual prompts and data and weighing performance and cost tradeoffs against use-case benchmarks.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered value decision: operationalize a transformation claim through adoption, decision-time, quality, and outcome gates instead of a launch proxy; distinct from the existing completion-rate diagnosis.

additions.scenario: A tax-appeal assistant must recall at least 97% of material exceptions. The efficient model reaches 91%, while a stronger model reaches 98% at four times the unit cost and remains under the asynchronous service deadline.
additions.evidence: The quality floor is measured on a held-out exception set; high-impact appeals are a minority and a human route remains available.
