existing.rationale: The accepted pair covers independent outcome and interaction evidence; each distractor violates isolation, flexibility, or validity.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Require one exact tool order or score only the final explanation.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Valid implementations can differ, and prose can claim success without changing the repository.
existing.counterfactual: If the task's only valid output were one canonical file with a deterministic checksum, a sequence rubric would add little value.
existing.sourceSection: Design the eval harness and graders
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends clean isolated trials, outcome-based grading, deterministic checks where possible, and calibrated model graders for nuanced dimensions.
existing.auditFinding: Preserve the independent deterministic-check and calibrated-review decision; replace exact-tool-order and explanation-only distractors with credible grader choices that each leave one evidence requirement unmet, and align feedback.

existing.scenario: A web-capable assistant is evaluated only on questions that should search, so it learns to search nearly every request.
existing.evidence: The team can add reviewed stable-fact cases and wants to expose both unnecessary searches and missed searches.
existing.decisiveConstraint: A trigger evaluation needs positive and negative cases and separate error classes.
existing.expectedDecision: Build a balanced set of cases that should search and cases that should answer directly, then grade each behavior separately.
existing.rationale: The transfer is pedagogically useful, but the keyed option is the only fully specified action and is longer than all distractors.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Add only more current-information questions or tune the threshold against the one-sided score.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Both reinforce over-triggering and never measure the missed-search or unnecessary-search boundary separately.
existing.counterfactual: If every supported request genuinely required current web data, a positive-only set would not create this trigger bias.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends testing cases where a behavior should occur and where it should not to avoid one-sided optimization.
existing.auditFinding: Underlying evaluation repair is valid, but the correct option is longer and more explicit than all alternatives; rewrite with plausible but one-sided dataset choices of comparable specificity.

additions.scenario: A claims extractor scores 100% after prompt tuning, but tuning fixtures and scored fixtures share templates and the suite has no provenance or frozen holdout. Production exposes unseen document layouts.
additions.evidence: The team can trace fixture origin, deduplicate near-identical cases, and run a known reference solution before freezing a new evaluation split; provenance, deduplication, and holdout separation are scenario-authored validity controls.
additions.decisiveConstraint: Cases used to tune the system cannot be the sole evidence for generalization; the holdout must represent unseen layouts and preserve a valid task/grader contract.
additions.expectedDecision: Separate tuning from a provenance-tracked, deduplicated holdout, validate it with a reference solution, and report results on the frozen holdout.
additions.rationale: This adds dataset provenance and holdout validity, absent from current mixed graders, broken path, clean trial, and balanced-trigger decisions. The cited anchor supports validating task and grader configuration with a reference solution; the holdout controls are the scenario's policy.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Keep the 100% score and add more copies of the same template to increase sample count.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: Duplicating tuned patterns increases apparent volume without testing the unseen document boundary.
additions.counterfactual: If the suite were a fixed deterministic contract with no tuning and all production layouts were represented, a separate holdout would add less evidence.
additions.sourceSection: Step 2: Write unambiguous tasks with reference solutions
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic says ambiguous specifications create noise and recommends a known working reference solution to verify that tasks and graders are configured correctly.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered decision: protect evaluation validity from tuned or duplicated fixtures by using provenance, deduplication, and a frozen holdout; current items do not test this boundary.

additions.scenario: A tool-using agent passes 9 of 10 trials on one run, then ranges from 5 to 9 on repeated runs of the same tasks because an external lookup is variable.
additions.evidence: The harness can record trial-level tool responses, transcripts, and outcomes and can distinguish deterministic checks from variable external state; repeated trials and distribution reporting are scenario-authored controls.
additions.decisiveConstraint: One favorable run cannot represent a stochastic or externally variable behavior; trial evidence must expose variance and the cause of failures.
additions.expectedDecision: Run repeated isolated trials, retain transcripts and tool-state evidence, and report the distribution or failure classes instead of only the best aggregate run.
additions.rationale: This adds repeatability and variance diagnosis to the dataset/framework design, distinct from choosing grader types or balancing trigger examples. The cited anchor establishes explicit trial and transcript evidence; the variance threshold and reporting rule are scenario premises.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Use the 9/10 result as the baseline and rerun only if users report failures.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: It confuses a favorable sample with stable capability and discards the trial evidence needed to explain variable outcomes.
additions.counterfactual: If every tool response and model run were deterministic and the reference solution passed, a single clean trial per case could be sufficient for this harness.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic defines evaluations through tasks, trials, graders, transcripts, outcomes, and a harness, which supports explicit evidence and ownership across lifecycle decisions.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered decision: distinguish stable capability from trial variance or variable tool state by preserving repeated trial evidence; current items do not require distribution-level interpretation.

additions.scenario: A model judge rates the same code explanations higher when they are longer and when the preferred answer is listed first; human reviewers disagree with that pattern.
additions.evidence: The harness can randomize option order, compare judge labels with calibrated human labels, and retain the underlying answers and rationales; randomization and verbosity probes are scenario-authored validity controls.
additions.decisiveConstraint: A judge cannot be trusted merely because it produces a score; order and verbosity bias must be measured and calibrated against the intended outcome.
additions.expectedDecision: Use deterministic checks for objective assertions, randomize presentation where order can bias judgment, calibrate the model rubric against human review, and escalate disagreement.
additions.rationale: This adds judge-bias and calibration validation, distinct from the current choice of mixed graders and task or repository harness validity. The cited anchor supports human calibration; the order and verbosity probes are supplied by the scenario.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Keep the judge because its average score is stable and ignore the order effect.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: A stable biased score can systematically reward verbosity or position instead of the required behavior.
additions.counterfactual: If every assertion had a deterministic checker and no model judgment were used, presentation order would not affect the evaluator.
additions.sourceSection: Design the eval harness and graders
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends deterministic graders where possible, model graders when necessary, and human review for validation and calibration.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered decision: validate model-judge bias from answer order or verbosity against calibrated human labels; existing rows select grader types but do not test evaluator bias.

additions.scenario: A coding agent must produce a correct read-only billing report. It first calls delete_customer with a real customer ID; the policy server denies the call, so no state changes. The agent then uses an allowed read query and returns the exact expected report, and all report tests pass.
additions.evidence: The transcript and tool audit record the denied destructive call, its real target, the policy denial, the valid read, and the correct final artifact. The evaluation contract says no unauthorized or destructive action may be attempted.
additions.decisiveConstraint: A correct final outcome does not erase an invalid intermediate action when the task contract includes a safety prohibition.
additions.expectedDecision: Fail the trial because the unauthorized destructive attempt violates its safety gate. Record correct-report outcome credit separately, while allowing harmless variation among authorized read-only paths.
additions.rationale: This tests a hybrid contract: process safety is a binary gate while the final report and permitted path remain outcome dimensions. It avoids requiring one brittle sequence for otherwise valid work.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Pass the trial because the server blocked the delete and the final report and tests are correct.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: A downstream denial is not evidence that the agent respected the contract; passing would hide attempted destructive behavior and reward unsafe tool selection.
additions.counterfactual: If the first call were an allowed read_customer operation with the same final report, the trial could pass because the varied sequence remains within the authorized action set.
additions.sourceSection: Design the eval harness and graders
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic lists tool-call verification among code-based graders, supports binary or hybrid scoring, and cautions that rigidly requiring one valid path is brittle; the prohibited-action gate is a scenario contract.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered evaluation decision: fail a run for an unauthorized intermediate tool action even when the final answer is correct, while preserving credit for valid path variation.

additions.scenario: An agent passes 99% of a 500-case evaluation, but only two cases exercise a high-impact destructive tool attempt and neither covers a negative case where the tool must be refused. The release owner asks whether the aggregate pass is sufficient.
additions.evidence: The tool-safety cases, ordinary cases, tool-call traces, and independent evaluator are available; the destructive behavior is governed by a separate guardrail.
additions.decisiveConstraint: A rare high-impact behavior needs balanced positive and negative cases before the aggregate can support release; ordinary-case volume cannot compensate for missing safety coverage.
additions.expectedDecision: Expand or hold out a risk-stratified set with both allowed and refused destructive-action cases, grade tool traces deterministically, and block the release until the safety slice passes its own gate.
additions.rationale: This reverses the existing mixed-grader selection, which can proceed with real and edge cases: here the edge behavior is too sparse to make that methodology representative.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Ship because 99% aggregate accuracy and ordinary-case tool traces pass, then monitor destructive attempts in production.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: Production monitoring would discover a high-blast-radius failure after release, and aggregate accuracy hides the missing trigger/refusal behavior.
additions.counterfactual: If the evaluation already contained a provenance-tracked, balanced high-impact slice with independent traces and passing safety gates, the ordinary aggregate could be combined with it for release.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends testing cases where a behavior should occur and where it should not to avoid one-sided optimization.
additions.integrationConstraint: ccarp-5.1 requires the guardrail to represent both the behavior that is allowed and the behavior that must be blocked; removing those cases changes the action from release to a safety hold.
additions.auditFinding: True reversal: high aggregate pass rate cannot authorize release when a rare destructive-action slice lacks balanced positive and negative evidence.

additions.scenario: A coding agent must produce a correct read-only billing report. In the original evaluation, one trial attempted delete_customer with a real ID before producing the report; a revised implementation now reaches the same report through a different fully authorized read-only lookup path, while the evaluator still expects the original tool sequence.
additions.evidence: Independent billing fixtures, final report fields, authorization traces, tool arguments, and the old gold trace are available; the revised path performs no write or destructive operation.
additions.decisiveConstraint: The safety and business contract requires a correct report without unauthorized side effects, not one incidental read-only call sequence; a changed authorized path should pass outcome and constraint grading unless the exact sequence is itself a declared requirement.
additions.expectedDecision: Pass the revised trial for the correct report and authorized read-only behavior, record the path variation, and update the gold trace or grader only if the sequence was never a contract; keep the destructive attempt as a separate failure evidence case.
additions.rationale: This is a true reversal of the existing unsafe-intermediate-action case: the old trial violated a safety gate, while the revised trial satisfies the outcome and authorization constraints despite a different harmless path.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Fail the revised trial because its tool trace differs from the historical gold sequence, even though the report and authorization checks pass.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: A historical path is not a business or safety requirement by itself; failing it would reward incidental implementation order and discourage safe authorized alternatives.
additions.counterfactual: If the task explicitly required one exact tool sequence for audit or side-effect ordering, the trace difference would be a contract failure and the trial would need remediation.
additions.sourceSection: Design the eval harness and graders
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends clean isolated trials, outcome-based grading, deterministic checks where possible, and calibrated model graders for nuanced dimensions.
additions.integrationConstraint: ccarp-5.1 requires the tool action to remain least-privilege and free of unauthorized side effects; because the revised path is fully read-only, the action changes from safety failure to outcome pass, while any write attempt remains a separate veto.
additions.auditFinding: True reversal: an unauthorized destructive intermediate action fails the existing safety case, but a different fully authorized read-only path with the correct outcome should pass unless exact sequence is an explicit contract.

objectiveLabel: Conduct A/B testing and iterative improvements

existing.scenario: A support team wants to test a new prompt against the live prompt for account-routed customer traffic while tracking resolution, escalation, latency, cost, and safety.
existing.evidence: Stable account assignment, sufficient traffic, predeclared metrics, and a safety stop rule are available.
existing.decisiveConstraint: The comparison must avoid treatment crossover and let safety override a quality lift.
existing.expectedDecision: Randomize eligible accounts, predefine primary and guardrail metrics, run a sufficient sample, and inspect slices and transcripts.
existing.rationale: The experimental design is valid, but the keyed option is the longest and most detailed; rewrite options with comparable scope and plausible sampling flaws.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Offer the prompt to volunteers or compare everyone after deployment with the prior week's traffic.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Self-selection and time-based controls confound prompt effect with user and traffic changes.
existing.counterfactual: If the change were a purely offline formatter with deterministic inputs, live randomized traffic would not be needed to estimate user impact.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends a small pilot, infrastructure for A/B testing, human feedback, and ongoing updates to offline evaluations from production data.
existing.auditFinding: Underlying experiment design is valid, but the keyed option is materially longer and more complete than every distractor; rewrite with parallel rollout and sampling choices.

existing.scenario: Prompt B lifts correct claim resolution from 82% to 86% but raises p95 latency 40%, cost 25%, and safety escalations in a high-risk category.
existing.evidence: Account assignment and category slices are recorded; the high-risk category has stricter safety tolerance.
existing.decisiveConstraint: A headline quality lift cannot override a safety regression or violated operating limit.
existing.expectedDecision: Inspect affected transcripts and trade-offs, keep safety/latency/cost as guardrails, and iterate or constrain B before rollout.
existing.rationale: The trade-off diagnosis is sound, but the correct option is much longer and more specific than the alternatives, creating a length cue.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Ship B on the overall resolution lift or average all four metrics into one score.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Averages hide severity and category effects and cannot make a hard safety breach acceptable.
existing.counterfactual: If B improved quality with no guardrail regression and every category shared the same risk tolerance, broad rollout could follow the predefined analysis.
existing.sourceSection: How evals fit with other methods for a holistic understanding of agents
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic says A/B tests measure real user outcomes but need transcript review to explain metric changes; multiple evaluation layers are complementary.
existing.auditFinding: Underlying diagnosis is valid, but the correct option is substantially longer and more operational than the distractors; rewrite with equally plausible rollout responses.

existing.scenario: A coding-agent model upgrade beats a small offline suite but can edit files and run commands in shared development environments.
existing.evidence: Sandboxed testing, a controlled canary, deterministic assignment, and rollback criteria are available.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Offline results and bounded live evidence answer different questions; exposure must remain reversible.
existing.expectedDecision: Use sandbox evaluation followed by a small canary or A/B cohort with quality, safety, latency, cost monitoring and rollback.
existing.rationale: The accepted pair cleanly separates prelaunch and live evidence and limits blast radius; distractors rely on scores or self-approval.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Roll out universally because the offline score is higher.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: It removes the control group and exposes shared environments before live behavior is known.
existing.counterfactual: If the model had no tools or side effects and the offline suite covered the full deterministic contract, a canary would add less safety evidence.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends starting with a small pilot, evaluating thoroughly, scaling gradually, and setting up A/B testing and human oversight.
existing.auditFinding: Preserve the small-pilot, oversight, and rollback decision; replace universal rollout and offline-score-only distractors with credible staged-exposure alternatives that each leave a guardrail or live-evidence requirement unmet, and align feedback.

existing.scenario: A document assistant produces three live failure patterns missing from its original offline suite; engineers propose fixing tickets individually and leaving the suite unchanged.
existing.evidence: Reports contain real inputs, can be triaged by impact, and reviewed cases can run in CI.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Production evidence must become repeatable regression evidence without replacing the curated core with unreviewed noise.
existing.expectedDecision: Triage reports, add representative regression cases with explicit graders, rerun fixes, and watch established behavior for regressions.
existing.rationale: The living-suite practice is correct, but the keyed option is much longer than all distractors and signals the answer by completeness.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Freeze the historical suite or replace it wholesale with the newest reports.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Freezing preserves blind spots; wholesale replacement loses stable coverage and imports duplicates or noise.
existing.counterfactual: If reports were unverified anecdotes with no reproducible inputs, they would need investigation before becoming evaluation cases.
existing.sourceSection: Maintain and use the eval long-term
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends treating evaluations as a living suite and combining them with production monitoring and feedback as systems evolve.
existing.auditFinding: Underlying transfer is valid, but the correct option is materially longer and more specific; rewrite with plausible but incomplete feedback-maintenance alternatives.

additions.scenario: An A/B test reports a 2% resolution lift after only one day, but the predeclared sample target is not met and the confidence range overlaps; guardrail data is sparse and uneven across account types.
additions.evidence: Assignment is stable, but the experiment owner can extend the run, preserve the analysis plan, and inspect account-type slices before changing exposure; the sample target, confidence rule, and stopping boundary are predeclared scenario controls.
additions.decisiveConstraint: The observed lift is insufficient evidence for a rollout when the planned sample and guardrail coverage are incomplete.
additions.expectedDecision: Continue to the predeclared sample or stop for a defined safety breach, then analyze planned slices and transcripts before declaring a winner.
additions.rationale: This adds evidence sufficiency and stopping-boundary reasoning, distinct from the existing account assignment and metric-tradeoff scenarios. The cited anchor supports real-user outcome and transcript evidence; the sample and stopping rule are scenario-authored.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Ship the new variant because the early point estimate is positive.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: An underpowered, uneven sample can turn noise or a segment effect into an unjustified global decision.
additions.counterfactual: If the experiment had completed its planned sample with stable guardrails and a prespecified stopping rule, the recorded effect could support the rollout decision.
additions.sourceSection: How evals fit with other methods for a holistic understanding of agents
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic says A/B tests measure real user outcomes but are slower and need transcript review to explain metric changes; multiple evaluation layers are complementary.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered decision: distinguish an early point estimate from a sufficiently observed A/B result and preserve predeclared stopping and slice analysis before rollout.

additions.scenario: Variant B reports a 4 percentage-point resolution lift over A. Assignment was intended to be account-level, but a routing bug sent 12% of users both variants; B also received twice as many easy premium accounts because the segment filter changed mid-run. Session and assignment logs preserve the crossover and composition data.
additions.evidence: The aggregate lift, treatment exposure, account segment, session ID, and outcome are available. The original plan requires clean account assignment and comparable segment mix before rollout.
additions.decisiveConstraint: A contaminated cohort and changed segment composition can create an apparent treatment effect even when the variant has no causal lift.
additions.expectedDecision: Do not declare B the winner; audit exposure and segment assignment, exclude or separately analyze contaminated sessions, restore balanced account-level randomization, and rerun the comparison before changing exposure.
additions.rationale: This is a causal-validity diagnosis, distinct from selecting metrics, waiting for an adequate sample, or inspecting a genuine quality and guardrail trade-off.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Post-hoc weight the aggregate results for the segment mix and ship B because the adjusted estimate remains positive.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: Weighting cannot repair users who saw both treatments or recover the missing counterfactual for contaminated sessions; the exposure mechanism must be corrected and measured again.
additions.counterfactual: If exposure logs show no crossover, segment proportions match the plan, and the completed sample meets the analysis rule, the observed lift can proceed to the predeclared rollout decision.
additions.sourceSection: How evals fit with other methods for a holistic understanding of agents
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic describes A/B testing as measuring real-user outcomes and controlling for confounds, while noting that sufficient traffic and transcript review are needed; the exposure and composition checks are scenario controls.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered experiment decision: diagnose segment-composition change and account or session contamination before treating an aggregate A/B lift as causal.

additions.scenario: An A/B test has a predeclared interim analysis at 1,000 eligible accounts, a stopping rule for a large reliable lift, and a safety guardrail. At the interim point, the sample target for the full study is not complete, but the predeclared lift and guardrails meet the documented decision boundary.
additions.evidence: The registered interim time, sample size, primary metric, uncertainty rule, guardrails, assignment log, and analysis output are immutable and available before the result is reviewed.
additions.decisiveConstraint: A prespecified interim rule with sufficient evidence permits the declared decision; the absence of the final sample target alone does not require continuing when the rule authorizes stopping.
additions.expectedDecision: Apply the registered interim rule, stop or advance exposure as it specifies, preserve the analysis and guardrail evidence, and report the decision as an interim-boundary outcome rather than an unplanned peek.
additions.rationale: This reverses the existing evidence-sufficiency case: that item lacks its sample target and stopping basis, while this case includes both and therefore permits a declared decision now.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Continue the experiment solely because the full sample target is incomplete, or declare a winner from the dashboard without applying the registered interim rule.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: The first ignores an authorized stopping boundary; the second ignores the registered analysis and creates the unplanned-peeking problem covered by the rejected path.
additions.counterfactual: If the interim rule were absent, the sample/uncertainty boundary unmet, or a safety guardrail breached, the experiment would continue or stop for the breach rather than declare this interim result.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends a small pilot, infrastructure for A/B testing, human feedback, and ongoing updates to offline evaluations from production data.
additions.integrationConstraint: ccarp-6.3 requires a declared latency/error or safety guardrail and breach owner; if the interim rule and owner are removed, the action changes from authorized stop/advance to continued evidence collection.
additions.auditFinding: True reversal: an explicit interim rule and sufficient evidence can authorize a decision before the full sample, whereas an unplanned dashboard look cannot.

additions.scenario: A/B assignment is account-level, but support agents use one shared response playbook that contains Variant B's new instruction for both cohorts. Customer outcomes improve in both arms while account assignment logs remain balanced. The same staff carry the learned Variant B instruction across account assignments even after the shared document changes.
additions.evidence: The playbook revision history, account assignment, agent exposure logs, and outcome transcripts are available; users in each arm can interact with the same support staff.
additions.decisiveConstraint: Balanced account assignment does not identify a treatment effect when a shared operational artifact carries the intervention across arms; the experiment must isolate or model the spillover before exposure changes.
additions.expectedDecision: Label or quarantine the contaminated observations and version the shared playbook, then rerun a controlled comparison using arm-specific or cluster assignment that addresses staff-carried exposure, or explicitly model residual interference. Preserve exposure and outcome evidence before drawing a treatment-effect conclusion.
additions.rationale: This is a spillover reversal of the existing randomized account-level experiment and differs from assignment contamination: the randomizer is correct, but operations transmit treatment between arms.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Keep the balanced assignment and credit B for the improvement because both cohorts received the same support volume.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: The shared playbook makes both cohorts partially treated, so the observed lift cannot be attributed to B and could conceal harm in the intended control.
additions.counterfactual: If playbooks and agent exposure were isolated by arm, account-level randomization could support the existing A/B decision with the planned transcript review.
additions.sourceSection: How evals fit with other methods for a holistic understanding of agents
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic says A/B tests measure real user outcomes but need transcript review to explain metric changes; multiple evaluation layers are complementary.
additions.integrationConstraint: ccarp-6.3 requires feedback and outcome evidence tied to the supported request class; if the playbook spills across arms, attribution is invalid and exposure must be isolated before updating the SLA or feedback loop.
additions.auditFinding: Integrated reversal: correct randomization cannot rescue a shared playbook that transmits treatment across cohorts; isolate operational exposure or model interference before rollout.

objectiveLabel: Diagnose system issues (prompt failure, hallucinations, model mismatch)

existing.scenario: A policy lookup rollout produces confident unsupported limits because one route exposes a truncated JSON field, while a complete-record replay passes on the same model and prompt.
existing.evidence: Raw tool response, serialized payload, and model-visible result can be compared across the affected and passing routes.
existing.decisiveConstraint: The investigation must test the changed evidence boundary before changing model or generation variables.
existing.expectedDecision: Trace schema and serialization, diff raw versus model-visible tool results, confirm truncation, and add a contract test for required fields.
existing.rationale: The payload diagnosis is correct, but the keyed option is much longer and more concrete than all distractors; rewrite options with comparable diagnostic scope.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Raise temperature, swap the model, or add a disclaimer before tracing the payload.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: None restores a missing policy field or isolates the route-specific cause.
existing.counterfactual: If raw and model-visible tool results were identical and the failure persisted across routes, generation or model behavior would become a stronger hypothesis.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends grounding factual responses in direct source text, verifying claims with citations, and restricting answers to supplied documents when appropriate.
existing.auditFinding: Underlying diagnosis is valid, but the correct option is the longest and most specific; rewrite all options as comparable hypotheses and evidence checks.

existing.scenario: Only a newly enabled infrastructure route produces corrupted characters and syntax errors after deployment; another route on the same model remains normal.
existing.evidence: The system can roll back and add a detector for the observed corruption; the symptom tracks route and deployment.
existing.decisiveConstraint: A route-correlated runtime regression should be contained and compared with a known-good path before prompt or model changes.
existing.expectedDecision: Compare route/runtime configuration, roll back or isolate the change, preserve evidence, and add a targeted detection test.
existing.rationale: The infrastructure diagnosis is strongly supported, but the keyed option is far longer than the distractors and gives away the cause.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Rewrite the prompt to forbid unusual characters or ask users to retry.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Prompt wording and retries do not explain or contain a route-specific serving corruption.
existing.counterfactual: If corruption occurred on every route only for one prompt family, a prompt or model compatibility investigation would precede rollback of shared infrastructure.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic describes a runtime deployment that caused corrupted characters and syntax errors, then reports rollback and detection tests for unexpected output.
existing.auditFinding: Underlying diagnosis is valid, but the correct option is materially longer and more actionable than the alternatives; rewrite with credible serving, prompt, and model hypotheses.

existing.scenario: A legal summarizer fails on long contracts; a larger model helps shorter contracts, while prompt revisions trade one clause type against another.
existing.evidence: The team can hold prompt or model constant and slice results by contract length and clause type, with transcripts and retrieved context.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Cause isolation requires a crossed matrix and trace inspection rather than simultaneous changes or aggregate scoring.
existing.expectedDecision: Cross prompts against candidate models and inspect representative context/transcripts by failing slice.
existing.rationale: The two accepted steps isolate model, prompt, and evidence-boundary effects; distractors change uncontrolled variables or hide slices.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Choose the best anecdotal answer or raise output limits for every request.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Neither identifies whether length, clause type, prompt, model, or missing evidence is causal.
existing.counterfactual: If one prompt and model failed uniformly across short and long contracts, a slice interaction matrix would be less necessary than a direct shared-input diagnosis.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic says not every failing evaluation is best solved by prompting; latency and cost, for example, may be improved more directly by model selection.
existing.auditFinding: Preserve crossed prompt/model/context cause isolation; replace anecdotal-answer and blanket-output-limit distractors with credible single-variable diagnostic choices that cannot identify the failing slice, and align feedback.

existing.scenario: A multilingual intake assistant begins refusing benign requests in one language after a policy prompt edit; both old and new model versions are available in staging.
existing.evidence: The prompt edit is the only known content change and the same language-specific inputs can be run across both models.
existing.decisiveConstraint: The team must distinguish a prompt regression from a model-by-prompt compatibility issue without weakening a safety boundary in production.
existing.expectedDecision: Run the same inputs across old/new prompts and old/new models, compare refusal and safety outcomes by language, and inspect traces.
existing.rationale: The two-by-two diagnostic is sound, but the keyed option is much longer than the alternatives; rewrite with parallel experimental choices.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Lower a refusal threshold in production or test only the newest model and prompt.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: The former risks safety; the latter cannot separate prompt and model interaction effects.
existing.counterfactual: If both model versions regressed with the old prompt too, the prompt edit would be exonerated and the investigation would move to shared policy or input handling.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends defining success criteria and having empirical tests before iterating on a prompt, rather than treating prompt changes as an unmeasured fix.
existing.auditFinding: Underlying diagnostic transfer is valid, but the correct option is substantially longer and more complete; rewrite choices with equally concrete two-variable investigations.

additions.scenario: A legal assistant gives an unsupported contract date in production. Replay with the same prompt and model is correct when the date clause is supplied, but the retriever omits that clause on affected documents.
additions.evidence: Retriever hit records, model-visible context, and a complete-context replay are available for the same document and query; the missing-context finding and retrieval repair are scenario-authored and cross-owned with D3.5/D3.6.
additions.decisiveConstraint: The answer is grounded only when the required evidence reaches the model; the first fix must target evidence presence and retrieval coverage rather than generation style.
additions.expectedDecision: Confirm whether the required clause is present in the model-visible evidence, repair retrieval or context assembly when it is absent, and rerun grounded-answer checks before changing the prompt or model.
additions.rationale: This isolates missing evidence from hallucination with a controlled context replay, a decision not covered by the current tool serialization and crossed prompt/model cases. The cited anchor supports grounding in supplied text; retrieval coverage and chunk repair are scenario-defined.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Add a stronger ‘do not hallucinate’ instruction or move immediately to a larger model.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: The controlled replay already shows the model can answer when evidence is present; wording or capability changes do not restore omitted evidence.
additions.counterfactual: If the required clause appeared in model-visible context and the same model still invented the date, generation grounding or model behavior would be the next hypothesis.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends grounding factual responses in direct source text and restricting answers to supplied documents when appropriate.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered decision: use evidence-presence replay to separate missing-context retrieval from model or prompt hallucination; current items diagnose serialization and model/prompt interactions but not this retrieval boundary.

additions.scenario: A legal assistant receives the complete current contract clause in model-visible context and cites the document, but it adds a renewal date that is not entailed by the clause and conflicts with a date in an adjacent section.
additions.evidence: The raw and model-visible evidence are identical, the citation span is available, and a claim-to-span check can test material fields before the answer is released.
additions.decisiveConstraint: Retrieval succeeded, but citation presence does not establish claim entailment; the generation layer must abstain or escalate when a material value is unsupported or contradicted.
additions.expectedDecision: Run claim-to-span and contradiction checks on the material date, mark the unsupported field unresolved, and route the answer for review rather than changing retrieval or selecting a larger model first.
additions.rationale: This reverses the existing retrieval-vs-generation item: the evidence is present here, so the next decision is entailment validation and abstention rather than repairing retrieval.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Accept the answer because the correct contract was retrieved and the response includes a citation, or fetch more documents until the model becomes confident.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: A citation can point to context without supporting the added value, and more context can compound conflicting dates instead of proving the claim.
additions.counterfactual: If the required clause were absent from model-visible context, the existing retrieval/context-repair decision would take priority before generation diagnosis.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends grounding factual responses in direct source text, verifying claims with citations, and restricting answers to supplied documents when appropriate.
additions.integrationConstraint: ccarp-5.5 requires a human review and limitation disclosure for consequential unsupported outputs; without that review path, the action changes from answer release to abstention.
additions.auditFinding: True reversal: complete retrieval and a citation do not make a material claim safe when the cited span does not entail it; validate and abstain at generation output.

objectiveLabel: Optimize token usage, latency, and cost-performance trade-offs

existing.scenario: Premium escalations need a high completeness floor; routine requests use a short schema and strict budget. A small model passes routine but misses premium, while routine outputs are verbose.
existing.evidence: Quality floors are measured separately, premium cannot be silently downgraded, and output tokens can be validated by workload.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Optimization must preserve each workload's floor while removing measured routine waste; a global cheapest model is invalid.
existing.expectedDecision: Route premium work to a model that passes its floor, tune a validated routine output budget, and recheck quality and spend by slice.
existing.rationale: The routing and token-budget decision is sound, but the keyed option is the longest and most detailed; rewrite choices with comparable action scope.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Route all work to the smaller model or raise the global output limit.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: The former violates premium completeness; the latter spends more on routine verbosity without proving quality.
existing.counterfactual: If both workloads passed the same quality floor on the small model and had the same latency contract, one shared budget could be defensible.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends reducing spend while preserving quality and identifies token hygiene as a way to remove unnecessary usage.
existing.auditFinding: Underlying optimization is valid, but the correct option is longest and conflates model choice with a detailed policy; rewrite with parallel measured alternatives and keep D04.5's quality-floor focus distinct from D02.1 capability selection.

existing.scenario: Prompt-cache reads fall from 88% to below 10% after a unique request timestamp is inserted at the front of an otherwise stable system prompt.
existing.evidence: The timestamp is only diagnostic metadata; document and policy content are unchanged and cache-write tokens spike.
existing.decisiveConstraint: A reusable prefix must remain byte stable; moving request-specific bytes must preserve observability without invalidating cache reuse.
existing.expectedDecision: Move the timestamp to request metadata or the newest user turn, then verify cache-read fields on repeated cases.
existing.rationale: The cache diagnosis is correct, but the keyed option is much longer and more operational than the distractors; rewrite with plausible TTL, model, and placement hypotheses.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Increase TTL or switch models while leaving the timestamp in the stable prefix.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: TTL and model size do not make different prefixes equal, so every request still misses the cache.
existing.counterfactual: If the prefix were unchanged and cache reads still fell, the team would inspect TTL, breakpoint, model, or cache availability rather than moving request metadata.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic says per-request text ahead of a stable prefix makes every request a full cache write and advises keeping moving text in the newest user turn.
existing.auditFinding: Underlying cache diagnosis is valid, but the correct option is materially longer and more specific; rewrite choices as comparable cache-placement and configuration hypotheses.

existing.scenario: A publisher generates 40,000 summaries overnight while a separate editor chat must remain interactive; quality floors cannot be lowered.
existing.evidence: Batch latency is acceptable for summaries, interactive latency matters for chat, and token/cache use can be measured.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Cost levers must match workload timing and preserve the evaluated quality contract.
existing.expectedDecision: Use batch processing for overnight work and measure/cache stable prefixes or token use on the interactive path while retaining quality floors.
existing.rationale: The two accepted changes apply distinct cost levers to distinct latency contracts; distractors either risk quality or destroy cacheability.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Use the least expensive model for all requests without quality comparison.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Untested model reduction can breach the summary floor and does not respect the split latency requirements.
existing.counterfactual: If all requests required immediate streaming, batch processing would violate the user contract and caching or token hygiene would be the available levers.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic identifies prompt caching and token hygiene as quality-preserving cost levers and notes that batch processing trades latency for its discount.
existing.auditFinding: Preserve workload-specific quality, cost, and latency routing; replace cheapest-model-for-all and token-only distractors with credible cost/quality/latency trade-offs that violate the stated floor or interaction target, and align feedback.

existing.scenario: An interactive compliance conversation needs fast first output, while a ten-minute reconciliation job can be polled later; both reuse policy and tool context.
existing.evidence: The consumers have different completion contracts and repeated stable context can be cached in each request shape.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Transport and execution mode must follow user latency and completion needs rather than one universal synchronous path.
existing.expectedDecision: Stream the interactive path, use asynchronous batch/polling for reconciliation, and cache stable repeated context separately in both shapes.
existing.rationale: The architecture is correct, but the keyed option is far longer and more specific than every alternative; rewrite with comparable transport choices.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Use one synchronous request and raise max_tokens, or batch the interactive request for lower cost.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: The first risks timeouts; the second delays the user and violates the interactive contract.
existing.counterfactual: If reconciliation had to return before the user leaves the page, it would need an interactive streaming path or a shorter bounded workflow rather than polling.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends streaming for long-running interactive requests and Message Batches for work that can be polled instead of holding an uninterrupted connection.
existing.auditFinding: Underlying transfer is valid, but the correct option is materially longer and more complete; rewrite choices with parallel transport and context-reuse trade-offs, keeping D04.5 distinct from D03.3 critical-path design.

additions.scenario: A support agent's cost per resolved case doubles while per-call input and output tokens look stable; traces show retries causing the same retrieval and validation tools to run repeatedly.
additions.evidence: The team can count tool calls and retry attempts per resolved case, compare successful versus failed loops, and set a maximum action or spend budget; the per-case budget and loop cap are scenario-authored controls.
additions.decisiveConstraint: The optimization target is cost per successful outcome, not tokens per individual call; repeated work must stop without lowering resolution quality.
additions.expectedDecision: Deduplicate or cache repeat tool work, bound retries and total agent steps, and re-evaluate cost per resolved case and quality after the change.
additions.rationale: This adds retry and tool-loop amplification as an operating-cost cause, distinct from current model routing, output limits, cache-prefix placement, and transport choices. The cited API anchor supports classifying and bounding retryable failures; tool-loop deduplication is scenario-specific engineering reasoning.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Switch to a cheaper model or shorten the response limit while leaving the retry loop unchanged.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: The measured waste is repeated tool execution; changing model or prose length leaves the amplification path and may reduce quality without lowering calls.
additions.counterfactual: If tool calls per resolved case were stable and cost rose with input tokens, context pruning or cache-prefix inspection would be the next optimization hypothesis.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic documents distinct error types, retry-after semantics, exponential backoff for transient failures, and a separate spend-cap condition that keeps failing until access resumes.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered decision: diagnose cost per outcome inflation from repeated tool work and bound retries/steps; current items cover model routing, token budgets, cache placement, and transport but not agent-loop amplification.

additions.scenario: A low-volume workflow has a short shared prefix and receives requests too far apart for repeated cache reads. Billing measurements show cache-write and cache-read charges plus setup latency are equal to or greater than uncached input cost, while quality is unchanged.
additions.evidence: Per-request input tokens, cache reads and writes, request spacing, setup latency, quality slices, and Usage API cost dimensions are available for a controlled before/after comparison.
additions.decisiveConstraint: Prompt caching is a cost lever only when a stable prefix is reused often enough to amortize its writes and reads; measured low reuse and a short prefix reverse the default optimization choice.
additions.expectedDecision: Disable caching for this low-volume short-prefix route, retain the stable prompt shape if it helps quality, and monitor uncached cost and latency against the same quality floor before reconsidering.
additions.rationale: This adds a cost-benefit reversal distinct from diagnosing a cache-breaking timestamp or designing multi-layer cache boundaries: the prefix is stable, but reuse economics are unfavorable.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Keep the cache on every route because stable prefixes are generally cheaper, or make the prefix longer by adding optional policy text.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: The stated billing measurements show no amortization, and adding optional text increases cache writes and context cost without improving quality.
additions.counterfactual: If traffic reused a long stable prefix frequently and cache-read savings exceeded writes and setup latency while quality stayed constant, caching would be the appropriate cost lever.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic identifies prompt caching and token hygiene as quality-preserving cost levers and notes that batch processing trades latency for its discount.
additions.auditFinding: New reversal: stable prefix alone does not justify caching when measured traffic cannot amortize cache writes, reads, and setup; retain the quality floor and decide from billing evidence.
additions.integrationConstraint: ccarp-4.6 requires provider usage and cost dimensions joined to route measurements; without read/write, spacing, and latency evidence, the action must remain a measured pilot rather than a global cache decision.

objectiveLabel: Monitor system performance using logging and observability tools

existing.scenario: An organization needs hourly and daily token trends by model and workspace, cached versus uncached input, cost attribution, capacity signals, and alerts across environments. Which data source should anchor accounting?
existing.evidence: Workspace boundaries are established. Provider-aligned usage dimensions are required for provider accounting; application capacity and request attribution are separate measures. Raw prompt storage is restricted.
existing.decisiveConstraint: The Usage API supplies provider token dimensions, while capacity and per-request attribution require application joins; missing joins must remain unknown rather than being replaced by estimates or prompt storage.
existing.expectedDecision: Use Usage API records grouped by model, workspace, and cache state for provider token accounting, then join request metadata to gateway capacity and approved cost records.
existing.rationale: Anchor provider accounting in Usage API records with model, workspace, and cache dimensions; join approved request metadata to gateway capacity and cost records, and flag unjoined attribution for follow-up.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Count characters in logs, keep only the monthly invoice, or store full prompts as a billing record.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Those choices lack provider tokenizer accuracy, workspace attribution, timely dimensions, or acceptable data minimization.
existing.counterfactual: If the requirement were only application latency and capacity diagnosis with no provider accounting, gateway traces could be primary and Usage API records secondary.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic's Usage API reports token consumption with filters and grouping by dimensions such as model and workspace, including cached and uncached input.
existing.auditFinding: Exam-preparation audit repair: Character estimates and monthly invoices cannot provide the required provider dimensions or hourly view; provider totals alone do not prove application capacity or per-request cost; storing prompts violates the data boundary.

existing.scenario: Average latency is stable while one region reports timeouts; request IDs, model/workspace, context and cache fields, region, and per-stage timings are retained.
existing.evidence: The symptom is a possible tail or segment effect hidden by global averages, and traces can correlate provider and application stages.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Diagnose the localized tail before a global timeout or model change masks the cause.
existing.expectedDecision: Slice p95/p99 by region, model, context, and cache state, correlate request IDs, and compare stage timings.
existing.rationale: The diagnostic sequence is sound, but the keyed option is the longest and most detailed; rewrite with equally concrete regional hypotheses.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Raise the global timeout, switch all regions to a larger model, or inspect only monthly cost.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Those actions mask impact or change unrelated variables and cannot locate the affected stage.
existing.counterfactual: If every region had the same p99 and only one model version regressed across all routes, a global model rollback would become a stronger next action.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic includes a unique request ID in responses and errors so operators can correlate a failing request with their own traces and support investigations.
existing.auditFinding: Underlying diagnosis is valid, but the correct option is materially longer and more complete; rewrite with parallel trace, timeout, and model hypotheses while keeping D04.6 monitoring distinct from D03.4 instrumentation design.

existing.scenario: A financial coaching assistant needs latency, errors, tokens, cache efficiency, and feedback, while privacy counsel rejects unrestricted raw-conversation storage.
existing.evidence: Structured fields can be retained, and sampled/redacted content can enter a separate controlled review path; the access and retention rules are scenario-provided privacy constraints.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Broad monitoring and sensitive transcript review need different access, retention, and purpose boundaries.
existing.expectedDecision: Emit structured request/model/workspace/timing/error/usage telemetry and use sampled or redacted transcripts plus linked feedback under access rules.
existing.rationale: The accepted pair cleanly separates operational signals from governed content review. The cited anchor supports complementary signals; access, retention, and redaction rules are scenario premises. The alternatives either over-collect or remove diagnosis.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Store every raw conversation forever or log only a success Boolean.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: The first violates the stated data boundary; the second cannot diagnose latency, usage, or quality failures.
existing.counterfactual: If conversations contained no sensitive fields and retention were unlimited, broad transcript retention could support deeper review, though structured metrics would still aid alerting.
existing.sourceSection: How evals fit with other methods for a holistic understanding of agents
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic describes production monitoring, user feedback, and manual transcript review as complementary ways to understand agent performance, each with different strengths and limits.
existing.auditFinding: Preserve structured telemetry plus sampled or redacted review traces; replace forever-raw and success-Boolean-only distractors with credible retention and diagnostic choices that lose either privacy or failure explainability, and align feedback.

existing.scenario: A shared API gateway must warn on burst traffic, workspace spend exhaustion, and repeated provider failures while retrying only recoverable conditions. What monitoring and response policy fits?
existing.evidence: Provider error types and retry-after are available. Usage and cost can be grouped by workspace. Spend-cap failures remain failing until access resumes.
existing.decisiveConstraint: The documented error classes determine retry eligibility, while the scenario requires separate burst, spend, and repeated-failure signals with an owner action; a spend cap remains failing and must be routed rather than retried.
existing.expectedDecision: Monitor burst/rate-limit utilization, workspace spend, and repeated failures separately; use retry-after with bounded backoff only for transient errors, and route threshold breaches or spend caps to named owners.
existing.rationale: Classify each response, apply retry-after and bounded exponential backoff only to documented transient conditions, emit separate workspace signals for burst or rate-limit utilization, spend exhaustion, and repeated failures, and route each threshold breach to its owner.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Retry all errors indefinitely or suppress provider errors until monthly reconciliation.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Indefinite retries amplify load and spend; suppression delays the evidence needed for a bounded response.
existing.counterfactual: If the provider documented every failure as transient with retry-after and the gateway had no spend-cap path, bounded exponential backoff could be the only recovery branch.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic documents distinct error types, retry-after semantics, exponential backoff for transient failures, and a separate spend-cap condition that keeps failing until access resumes.
existing.auditFinding: Exam-preparation audit repair: Daily aggregation can miss a burst or rate-limit event; a shared backoff path cannot clear a persistent spend cap; and increasing retries without classification amplifies cost and traffic.

additions.scenario: Provider usage, latency, and error dashboards remain green, but sampled reviewers report a sharp drop in grounded answers for a newly introduced document type.
additions.evidence: The team can link redacted samples and outcome labels to request traces and can distinguish the new document slice without retaining all conversation content; governed sampling and the quality trigger are scenario-authored controls.
additions.decisiveConstraint: Operational health does not prove task quality; monitoring must detect slice drift and trigger a reviewable evaluation response under the data boundary.
additions.expectedDecision: Alert or investigate on the affected quality slice, retain governed representative traces, add reviewed cases to the evaluation loop, and keep provider usage metrics separate from task quality.
additions.rationale: This adds production quality-drift monitoring, distinct from current provider usage accounting, tail latency diagnosis, privacy-safe instrumentation, and error retry policy. The cited anchor supports combining evaluation with production monitoring and review; the slice trigger and retention method are scenario premises.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Declare the release healthy because usage and latency dashboards are green.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: Infrastructure and spend signals cannot detect a content-grounding regression on a new slice.
additions.counterfactual: If the new document type had no user-facing quality requirement and only provider capacity mattered, usage and latency could be sufficient operational signals.
additions.sourceSection: How evals fit with other methods for a holistic understanding of agents
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends combining automated evals with production monitoring, feedback, A/B tests, and transcript review for a holistic view.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered decision: detect quality drift when operational dashboards remain healthy and route governed production evidence into evaluation; current rows monitor provider and runtime signals but do not test this split.

additions.scenario: The overnight dashboard shows zero errors and normal spend, but the telemetry exporter for eu-west stopped sending data 42 minutes ago. The load balancer records 15,000 requests in that region, while application spans and quality labels are absent. The on-call runbook has a telemetry owner and a service owner.
additions.evidence: Exporter heartbeat, last-sample time, request counts, and alert routing are available. An empty error series is distinguishable from a fresh series whose request count reconciles with the gateway.
additions.decisiveConstraint: Missing or stale telemetry cannot establish service health; an alert must carry scope, freshness, evidence, owner, and an actionable next step.
additions.expectedDecision: Mark eu-west health unknown, page the telemetry owner with the stale interval and request-count evidence, and open the service investigation if the gap cannot be repaired promptly; do not close the event as green.
additions.rationale: This adds the alert contract and data-availability diagnosis to existing metric slicing and quality-drift monitoring. It concerns monitoring response and ownership, not trace schema design.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Suppress application-quality alerts until the exporter is restored and use fresh provider spend and error panels as the service-health signal during the gap.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: Provider usage panels do not show the missing regional application spans or task outcomes; relying on them hides unknown service health instead of explicitly escalating the telemetry gap.
additions.counterfactual: If the exporter heartbeat were current and gateway, application, and quality counts reconciled to zero errors for the interval, the dashboard could remain quiet without an unknown-health alert.
additions.sourceSection: How evals fit with other methods for a holistic understanding of agents
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic distinguishes production monitoring, which reveals live behavior but can be noisy and lacks grading ground truth, from evaluation and review; freshness, ownership, and alert payload requirements are scenario controls.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered monitoring decision: treat stale or missing telemetry as unknown health and route an evidence-backed alert to an owner instead of interpreting a quiet dashboard as healthy.

additions.scenario: The Usage API reports normal hourly tokens by workspace and model, but the application cannot map those totals to case IDs because one gateway route drops the trace key. A quality regression is reported for one workflow class.
additions.evidence: Provider usage dimensions, gateway route logs, request traces from healthy routes, and the affected case set are available; cached and uncached input are reported only at provider aggregation level.
additions.decisiveConstraint: Provider totals can account for spend but cannot attribute a quality regression to cases without an application-level join; missing joins must remain explicitly unknown rather than inferred from aggregate spend.
additions.expectedDecision: Repair the gateway trace key and reconcile provider usage to application cases for the affected route, report unattributed usage separately, and investigate quality using the joined traces and reviewed cases.
additions.rationale: This integrates provider accounting with application observability and adds a missing-attribution boundary beyond the existing usage dashboard and tail-segment rows.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Divide workspace token totals by the number of cases and estimate the affected class's cost and quality from the aggregate dashboard.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: Average allocation hides route-specific retries, cache state, and case mix, so it cannot explain the quality regression or support a cost-per-outcome decision.
additions.counterfactual: If every route preserved a stable case/request key and the Usage API dimensions reconciled to the application ledger, aggregate usage could be used with the existing slice dashboards.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic's Usage API reports token consumption with filters and grouping by dimensions such as model and workspace, including cached and uncached input.
additions.integrationConstraint: ccarp-3.4 requires correlated traces across retrieval, model, and application stages; without a stable case/request key, provider usage cannot be reconciled to task outcomes and unknown attribution must remain.
additions.auditFinding: Integrated family: provider Usage API aggregation is insufficient for case-level diagnosis when the application join key is missing; repair correlation and surface unknown attribution.

objectiveLabel: Implement guardrails and safety controls

existing.scenario: A procurement assistant reads an untrusted vendor email, drafts purchase orders, and must not disclose a supplier list or submit a purchase without approval. Which guardrail design is appropriate?
existing.evidence: The email contains an indirect instruction. The supplier list is unnecessary to draft the order. Submission is a consequential write action.
existing.decisiveConstraint: The design isolates attacker-controlled content, removes unnecessary supplier-list access, limits the assistant to drafting, and places an enforceable approval boundary before the write.
existing.expectedDecision: Keep the email in an identified untrusted tool_result, screen its fields, omit supplier-list data and access, allow draft-only tools, and require approval before submission.
existing.rationale: Pass the email as identified untrusted data, screen the proposed fields, provide no supplier-list data or lookup authority, expose only drafting tools, and require accountable confirmation before submission.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Put the email in the system prompt, give the agent the supplier list, and rely on a caution sentence.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: Those choices promote attacker text, expand blast radius, or rely on wording instead of enforceable authority boundaries.
existing.counterfactual: If the content were trusted internal policy and the assistant had no sensitive-data or write access, tool-result isolation and a submission approval gate would carry less operational value.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends isolating third-party content in tool_result blocks, screening tool outputs, and limiting sensitive data and actions with least privilege.
existing.auditFinding: Exam-preparation audit repair: System instructions promote attacker text, broad supplier or payment access expands blast radius, plain-text conversion does not remove the instruction threat, and a warning or later review cannot replace least privilege and pre-write approval.

existing.scenario: An accounts-payable classifier follows malicious OCR text and attempts a payment-tool call; OCR was concatenated into a normal user message and the agent has payment write access.
existing.evidence: The attack path combines an untrusted-data message construction error with unnecessary high-impact authority.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Fix both the content trust boundary and the privilege boundary before tuning model behavior.
existing.expectedDecision: Use an identified untrusted tool result, screen OCR, remove payment write access from classification, and rerun injection tests.
existing.rationale: The diagnosis is correct, but its answer is the longest and most actionable; rewrite options with comparable two-cause investigations.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Retain OCR as ordinary user text and leave payment write access enabled, while adding only a prompt warning about hostile content.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: That single design leaves both the untrusted-content boundary and the high-impact privilege boundary open; a warning is not application enforcement.
existing.counterfactual: If OCR were generated from a trusted internal source and the classifier had no side-effect tools, prompt construction would be a lower-risk quality concern.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic distinguishes indirect injection in documents and tool results and recommends structured untrusted results, output screening, and narrow permissions.
existing.auditFinding: Underlying diagnosis is valid, but the keyed correction is materially longer and more specific than the alternatives; rewrite with equally credible content-boundary and privilege hypotheses.

existing.scenario: A treasury assistant proposes vendor payments, but prompt injection could trigger an unaudited external payment.
existing.evidence: The team can require confirmation at the side-effect boundary, screen untrusted content, red-team, monitor, and keep payment authority narrow.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Consequential actions need an application-enforced approval boundary plus layered defenses against bypass and blast radius.
existing.expectedDecision: Require explicit human confirmation and a narrow policy-checked payment action; screen, red-team, and monitor the workflow.
existing.rationale: The accepted pair combines independent prevention, authorization, and detection controls; distractors rely on obscurity, broad credentials, or one prompt.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Grant broad payment authority and depend on a friendly system prompt.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: A probabilistic instruction does not constrain an irreversible tool call or provide evidence when it is bypassed.
existing.counterfactual: If the assistant only produced a reversible draft with no payment capability, human confirmation could move to the later application action.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends layering input and tool-output screening, hardened instructions, confirmation, least privilege, red-teaming, and continuous monitoring.
existing.auditFinding: Preserve layered screening, least privilege, and approval at the payment boundary; replace broad-authority/friendly-prompt distractors with a credible policy-enforced alternative that still leaves an action or evidence boundary open, and align feedback.

existing.scenario: A contract assistant has no write tools but can reveal proprietary negotiation terms from a long system prompt when users ask for hidden instructions.
existing.evidence: Only task-relevant context is needed; outputs can be filtered and representative interactions audited, with quality degradation monitored.
existing.decisiveConstraint: Leak prevention is risk reduction: minimize exposed data, add output controls and audits, and measure harm to legitimate task quality.
existing.expectedDecision: Reduce unnecessary proprietary context, separate instructions from queries, filter outputs, and audit leakage and quality.
existing.rationale: The control plan is correct, but the keyed option is substantially longer and more complete than the distractors; rewrite with parallel leak-reduction strategies.
existing.plausibleAlternative: Add all proprietary detail and rely on forceful instructions or model refusals alone.
existing.whyAlternativeLoses: More exposed context enlarges the leak surface and neither refusal wording nor model size is a complete output boundary.
existing.counterfactual: If no proprietary context entered the model and outputs contained only public facts, leak filtering would not be needed for this path.
existing.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends separating context, removing unnecessary proprietary details, filtering outputs, and auditing regularly while testing for performance degradation.
existing.auditFinding: Underlying transfer is valid, but the correct option is far longer and more specific; rewrite with plausible controls of comparable scope and preserve the distinction from prompt-only guardrails.

additions.scenario: A research agent has only a read-only HTTP fetch tool, yet a malicious page instructs it to place case text in an image URL. The team assumes no write tool means no meaningful side effect.
additions.evidence: A proxy records arbitrary destinations and query strings; the deployment can use an egress allowlist, strip query data, and test a canary secret in fetched content. Those proxy and canary controls are scenario-provided application enforcement.
additions.decisiveConstraint: Read-only retrieval can still exfiltrate data through network output, so the egress channel and sensitive context need independent controls.
additions.expectedDecision: Keep fetched content untrusted, enforce an egress allowlist and URL/query policy, minimize secrets in context, and test the proxy against URL-based exfiltration.
additions.rationale: This adds a concrete network exfiltration guardrail for a read-only tool, distinct from broad threat mapping, prompt-leak filtering, and approval placement. The cited anchor supports untrusted-content isolation and least privilege; the egress and URL controls are scenario-authored.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Leave outbound URLs unrestricted because the agent cannot write to the source system.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: The model can transmit data through a permitted request even when it cannot mutate the source, so read-only authority does not remove the egress side channel.
additions.counterfactual: If the agent used an offline local corpus with no network-capable tool or egress path, URL filtering would be unnecessary and content isolation would address the remaining injection risk.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends isolating third-party content in tool_result blocks, screening tool outputs, and limiting sensitive data and actions with least privilege.
additions.auditFinding: Uncovered decision: constrain and test network egress even for read-only tools because untrusted content can turn requests into an exfiltration channel; current rows do not isolate this side effect.

additions.scenario: A payment assistant has correctly screened an untrusted invoice and prepared a narrow draft, but the screening service becomes unavailable immediately before the payment action. The draft is still awaiting accountable confirmation.
additions.evidence: The screening dependency status, untrusted invoice, draft parameters, confirmation state, and side-effect action are recorded; the payment tool is otherwise available.
additions.decisiveConstraint: A required safety layer is unavailable at the side-effect boundary, so the workflow must fail closed even though the content was screened earlier and a confirmation is pending.
additions.expectedDecision: Hold or quarantine the draft, emit an explicit dependency-unavailable state, notify the payment owner, and submit only after screening and confirmation are revalidated.
additions.rationale: This adds a fail-closed dependency decision to the existing layered guardrails; the choice changes because a required control is unavailable at execution time.
additions.plausibleAlternative: Submit after the existing confirmation because the invoice was screened before the outage, or bypass screening for low-value payments.
additions.whyAlternativeLoses: The state may have changed after screening and the scenario defines screening as a required control; bypassing it turns an availability failure into an unobserved side effect.
additions.counterfactual: If screening were advisory, the action had no external effect, and the policy owner explicitly accepted that degraded mode, a documented unavailable state could be advisory rather than a hard hold.
additions.sourceClaim: Anthropic recommends layering input and tool-output screening, hardened instructions, confirmation, least privilege, red-teaming, and continuous monitoring.
additions.integrationConstraint: ccarp-5.3 requires accountable confirmation at the point of a high-value side effect; removing the available screening evidence changes the action from pending hold to an unsafe submission and is therefore disallowed.
additions.auditFinding: True reversal: when a required screening layer is unavailable at execution, layered safeguards require an explicit hold rather than treating prior screening or confirmation as sufficient.

additions.scenario: A high-value invoice is correctly isolated as untrusted content, but the input screen flags a new benign OCR format as a possible injection and provides no confidence or evidence for the flag. The payment tool is available and the accountable reviewer is waiting.
additions.evidence: The screen result, OCR fixture, prior false-positive rate, invoice provenance, tool permissions, and reviewer identity are available; no payment has been submitted.
additions.decisiveConstraint: A false-positive safety signal must not be silently bypassed or treated as proof of an attack; the high-value side effect needs a visible hold, calibrated evidence, and an accountable review path.
additions.expectedDecision: Keep the invoice quarantined, show the reviewer the flagged span and uncertainty, run the approved false-positive/benign fixture checks, and recalibrate or route the screen for review before any payment action.
